title.en: Volume 124 Treatises 99: Food and Money 5, Coinage, Tea Administration, Mining Administration
title.raw: 卷124 志九十九 食货五 钱法 茶法 矿政

sentences.zh: 志九十九

translations.literal: Treatise 99
translations.idiomatic: Treatise 99

sentences.zh: =食貨五=

translations.literal: [= Food and Money 5 =]
translations.idiomatic: Food and Money, Part Five

sentences.zh: 錢法太祖初鑄「天命通寶」錢，別以滿、漢文為二品，滿文一品錢質較漢文一品為大。

translations.literal: On coinage: At the beginning Taizu first cast Tianming Tongbao coins, distinguishing Manchu and Han script as two grades; the Manchu-script first grade was larger than the Han-script first grade.
translations.idiomatic: On coinage: In his early reign Taizu first cast Tianming Tongbao coins in two denominations distinguished by Manchu and Han inscriptions; the Manchu-inscription coin was the larger of the two.

sentences.zh: 天聰因之。

translations.literal: The Tiancong reign followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The Tiancong reign continued the same arrangement.

sentences.zh: 世祖定鼎燕京，大開鑄局，始定一品。

translations.literal: When Shizu established the capital at Yanjing, he greatly expanded the mints and for the first time fixed a single denomination.
translations.idiomatic: After Shunzhi made Beijing the capital, minting was greatly expanded and a single standard denomination was adopted.

sentences.zh: 於戶部置寶泉局，工部置寶源局。

translations.literal: At the Board of Revenue he established the Baoquan Bureau; at the Board of Works, the Baoyuan Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: The Baoquan mint was placed under the Board of Revenue and the Baoyuan mint under the Board of Works.

sentences.zh: 「順治通寶」錢，定制以紅銅七成、白銅三成搭配鼓鑄。

translations.literal: For Shunzhi Tongbao coins, the prescribed alloy was seventy percent red copper and thirty percent white copper, cast by the drum method.
translations.idiomatic: Shunzhi Tongbao coins were specified to be cast from an alloy of seventy parts red copper to thirty parts brass.

sentences.zh: 錢千為萬，二千串為一卯，年鑄三十卯。

translations.literal: One thousand cash made ten thousand; two thousand strings formed one mao; thirty mao were cast per year.
translations.idiomatic: One thousand coins counted as ten thousand for accounting; two thousand strings constituted one production cycle (mao), and thirty such cycles were minted annually.

sentences.zh: 每錢重一錢。

translations.literal: Each coin weighed one mace.
translations.idiomatic: Each coin weighed one mace (about 3.8 grams).

sentences.zh: 二年，增重二分，定錢七枚准銀一分，舊錢倍之。

translations.literal: In the second year, the weight was increased by two fen; seven new coins were fixed to equal one fen of silver; old coins counted double.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi year 2 the weight was raised by two fen, seven new coins were set equal to one fen of silver, and old coins counted at half that rate.

sentences.zh: 民間頗病錢貴，已更定十枚准一分。

translations.literal: The populace greatly suffered from the high price of cash, so it was changed to ten coins per fen of silver.
translations.idiomatic: Because the public found cash too dear, the rate was revised to ten coins per fen of silver.

sentences.zh: 各省、鎮遵式開鑄，先後開山西、陝西、密雲、薊、宣、大同、延綏、臨清、盛京、江西、河南、浙江、福建、山東、湖廣及荊州、常德、江寧三府鑄局。

translations.literal: Provinces and garrisons opened mints according to the standard; in succession mints were opened in Shanxi, Shaanxi, Miyun, Ji, Xuan, Datong, Yansui, Linqing, Shengjing, Jiangxi, Henan, Zhejiang, Fujian, Shandong, Huguang, and the three prefectures of Jingzhou, Changde, and Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: Provinces and garrison towns opened mints to the prescribed standard; over time mints were established in Shanxi, Shaanxi, Miyun, Ji, Xuanfu, Datong, Yansui, Linqing, Shengjing, Jiangxi, Henan, Zhejiang, Fujian, Shandong, Huguang, and the prefectures of Jingzhou, Changde, and Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 五年，停盛京、延綏二局。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, the two bureaus at Shengjing and Yansui were closed.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 the Shengjing and Yansui mints were shut down.

sentences.zh: 六年，移大同局於陽和。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, the Datong bureau was moved to Yanghe.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 the Datong mint was relocated to Yanghe.

sentences.zh: 七年，開襄陽、鄖陽二府鑄局。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, mint bureaus were opened in the two prefectures of Xiangyang and Yunyang.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 mints were opened in the prefectures of Xiangyang and Yunyang.

sentences.zh: 八年，停各府、鎮鑄。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, minting at all prefectures and garrisons was halted.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 provincial and garrison minting was suspended.

sentences.zh: 十年，復開密雲、薊、宣、陽和、臨清鑄局。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, the mint bureaus at Miyun, Ji, Xuan, Yanghe, and Linqing were reopened.
translations.idiomatic: In year 10 the Miyun, Ji, Xuanfu, Yanghe, and Linqing mints were reopened.

sentences.zh: 初戶部以新鑄錢足用，前代惟崇禎錢仍暫行，餘准廢銅輸官，償以直，並禁私鑄及小錢、偽錢，更申舊錢禁。

translations.literal: Initially the Board of Revenue held that newly cast coins were sufficient; only Chongzhen coins from the previous dynasty were temporarily allowed; the rest might be surrendered as scrap copper to the government for compensation at fair value; private casting, small coins, and counterfeit coins were forbidden, and the ban on old coins was renewed.
translations.idiomatic: At first the Board of Revenue judged the new coinage sufficient; only Chongzhen coins from the Ming were temporarily permitted to circulate, while other old copper had to be surrendered to the state for compensation, and private minting, small coins, and counterfeits were banned along with a renewed prohibition on old currency.

sentences.zh: 嗣以輸官久不盡，通令天下，限三月期畢輸，逾限行使，罪之。

translations.literal: Later, because surrender to the government was long incomplete, an order went out to the whole empire limiting delivery to three months; use after the deadline was punishable.
translations.idiomatic: When surrender lagged, an empire-wide order set a three-month deadline for delivery; anyone who continued to use old coin after that was liable to punishment.

sentences.zh: 是年廷議疏通錢法，以八年增重一錢二分五釐為定式，幕左漢文「一釐」二字，右寶泉鑄一字曰「戶」，寶源曰「工」，各省、鎮並鑄開局地名一字，如太原增「原」字、宣府增「宣」字之類，錢千准銀一兩，定為畫一通行之制。

translations.literal: That year the court debated easing the coinage system; the weight increase of year eight to one mace two fen five li was fixed as the standard; on the reverse, left in Han script were the two characters "one li," and right: Baoquan cast one character "Revenue," Baoyuan "Works," and provinces and garrisons each cast one character for the mint locality, as Taiyuan adding "Yuan" or Xuanfu adding "Xuan"; one thousand cash equaled one tael of silver, established as a uniform circulating system.
translations.idiomatic: That year the court debated reform of the currency. The weight adopted in year 8—one mace two fen five li—became the standard. The reverse bore the Han characters for "one li" on the left; Baoquan coins showed the character for Revenue (hu), Baoyuan for Works (gong), and provincial mints one character for the locality, as Taiyuan with yuan or Xuanfu with xuan. One thousand cash equaled one tael of silver, fixed as the uniform standard of circulation.

sentences.zh: 禁私局，犯者以枉法贓論。

translations.literal: Private mints were forbidden; offenders were judged under the statute on corrupt seizure of goods by officials.
translations.idiomatic: Private mints were outlawed; offenders were prosecuted under the statute on official corruption.

sentences.zh: 時官錢壅滯，通以斂散法，酌定京、外局錢，配搭俸餉。

translations.literal: At the time official cash was congested; the method of contraction and release was applied generally, apportioning capital and provincial mint coins to pay salaries.
translations.idiomatic: Official coin had piled up in treasury, so a contraction-and-release policy was applied, allocating mint output from Beijing and the provinces to salary payments.

sentences.zh: 錢糧舊制徵銀七錢三，皆著為令。

translations.literal: The old system of grain tax collection at seven mace three of silver per picul was all written into regulations.
translations.idiomatic: The old grain-tax rate of seven mace three of silver per picul was codified in regulations.

sentences.zh: 而直省局錢不精，私鑄乘之，卒壅不行，悉罷鑄，專任寶泉、寶源，精造一錢四分重錢，幕用滿文，俾私鑄艱於作偽。

translations.literal: But provincial mint coins were not refined; private casting took advantage, and in the end they clogged circulation; all provincial minting was abolished, leaving only Baoquan and Baoyuan to cast carefully coins of one mace four fen weight, with Manchu script on the reverse, so that private casting would find forgery difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial mints produced inferior coin, inviting counterfeiting until circulation stalled entirely. Provincial minting was abolished; only Baoquan and Baoyuan were retained to cast refined coins of one mace four fen with Manchu reverse inscriptions, making private forgery harder.

sentences.zh: 現行錢限三月銷毀。

translations.literal: Coins then in circulation were limited to three months before destruction.
translations.idiomatic: Coins then in circulation had to be withdrawn and melted within three months.

sentences.zh: 更定私鑄律，為首及匠人罪斬決，財產沒官，為從及知情買使，總甲十家長知情不首，地方官知情，分別坐斬絞，告奸賞銀五十兩。

translations.literal: The statute on private casting was revised: ringleaders and craftsmen were sentenced to decapitation and property confiscated; accomplices and knowing purchasers were punished by degrees; neighborhood heads and ten-household chiefs who knew but did not report, and local officials who knew, received decapitation or strangulation by degree; informants were rewarded fifty taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: Penalties for private minting were tightened: ringleaders and craftsmen were beheaded and their property confiscated; accomplices and knowing buyers were punished by degree, as were neighborhood heads and ten-household chiefs who failed to report and local officials who knew but did nothing. Informants received fifty taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 十七年，復直省鑄，令准重錢式，幕兼用滿、漢文。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, provincial minting was restored, ordered to follow the heavy-coin standard, with both Manchu and Han script on the reverse.
translations.idiomatic: In year 17 provincial minting resumed on the heavy-coin standard, with both Manchu and Han on the reverse.

sentences.zh: 康熙元年，鑄紀元錢，後凡嗣位改元，皆鑄如例。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kangxi, reign-title coins were cast; thereafter whenever a successor took the throne and changed the reign title, casting followed the precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 1 reign-title coins were introduced; thereafter every new reign cast coins in the same way.

sentences.zh: 高宗內禪，鑄乾隆錢十二，嘉慶錢十八，非常例也。

translations.literal: When Gaozong abdicated in favor of an heir, twelve Qianlong coins and eighteen Jiaqing coins were cast—an exceptional case.
translations.idiomatic: When Qianlong abdicated in favor of Jiaqing, twelve Qianlong denominations and eighteen Jiaqing denominations were cast—an exceptional departure from precedent.

sentences.zh: 自改鑄一錢四分錢，奸民輒私銷，乃定律罪之比私鑄。

translations.literal: From the change to casting one-mace-four-fen coins, wicked men constantly melted them privately; therefore the law fixed penalties equal to private casting.
translations.idiomatic: Once the one-mace-four-fen coin was introduced, illicit melting became common, and the law made clandestine melting punishable on the same terms as private minting.

sentences.zh: 遂禁造銅器，為私銷也。

translations.literal: Thus the manufacture of copper vessels was forbidden, to stop private melting.
translations.idiomatic: Copperware manufacture was therefore banned to curb illicit melting.

sentences.zh: 十八年，申嚴其禁，軍器、樂器之屬，許造用五斤以下者。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year the ban was strictly renewed; military weapons, musical instruments, and the like were permitted only if under five jin in weight.
translations.idiomatic: In year 18 the ban was tightened; only military weapons, musical instruments, and similar items under five jin were exempt.

sentences.zh: 時重錢銷益少，直苦昂。

translations.literal: At the time heavy coins were melted less and less, and their value painfully rose.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy coins were melted less often, and their value rose painfully.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，允錢法侍郎陳廷敬糾復一錢舊制。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, the memorial of Vice Minister of Coinage Chen Tingjing to restore the old one-mace standard was approved.
translations.idiomatic: In year 23 the court approved Vice Minister Chen Tingjing's memorial to restore the one-mace standard.

sentences.zh: 久之，錢貴如故，乃申定錢直禁，銀一兩易錢毋得不足一千，然錢直終不能平。

translations.literal: After a long time cash was dear as before; therefore a ban on the price of cash was renewed: one tael of silver must not buy fewer than one thousand cash; yet the price of cash could never be stabilized.
translations.idiomatic: Cash soon became dear again. A price floor was reissued: one tael of silver must buy at least one thousand cash—but the exchange rate never stabilized.

sentences.zh: 季年銀一兩易錢八百八十至七百七十。

translations.literal: In the late years of the reign one tael of silver exchanged for eight hundred eighty to seven hundred seventy cash.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of the reign one tael bought only 880 to 770 cash.

sentences.zh: 乃發五城平糶錢易銀以平其價。

translations.literal: Therefore relief grain funds from the Five Wards were released to sell cash for silver and level the price.
translations.idiomatic: Relief funds from the Five Wards were used to sell cash for silver in order to stabilize the rate.

sentences.zh: 自舊錢申禁，而閩地僻遠，猶雜制錢行之。

translations.literal: Since the ban on old coins was renewed, yet Fujian was remote, miscellaneous old coins still circulated there.
translations.idiomatic: Although old coin had been banned again, remote Fujian still circulated mixed old currency.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，巡撫金鋐以為言，學士徐乾學疏稱：「自古皆古今錢相兼行使，聽從民便。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year Governor Jin Qiao reported this; Academician Xu Qianxue memorialized: "From antiquity old and new coins have always circulated together, following popular convenience."
translations.idiomatic: In year 24 Governor Jin Qiao raised the issue. Academician Xu Qianxue memorialized: "From antiquity old and new coin have circulated side by side for the people's convenience."

sentences.zh: 」因曆數歷代舊事，謂「自漢五銖以來，未嘗廢古而專用今。

translations.literal: " He enumerated precedents from successive dynasties, saying: "Since the Han wushu coin, antiquity has never been abolished in favor of the present alone."
translations.idiomatic: He cited historical precedents: "Since the Han wushu, no dynasty has abolished old coin in favor of the new alone."

sentences.zh: 隋銷古錢，明天啟後盡括古錢充鑄，錢之變也。

translations.literal: The Sui melted old coins; after Tianqi in the Ming all old coins were seized for recasting—these were transformations of the currency.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui melted old coin; after Tianqi the Ming seized all old coin for recasting—each was a disruption of the currency.

sentences.zh: 且錢法敝，可資古錢以澄汰，故易代仍聽流通。

translations.literal: Moreover, when the coinage system is debased, old coins can serve to clarify and sift, so at dynastic change circulation is still permitted.
translations.idiomatic: When the currency is debased, old coin can help sift out bad money, which is why each new dynasty has allowed old coin to circulate.

sentences.zh: 矧閩處嶺外，宜聽民行使」。

translations.literal: How much more should Fujian beyond the mountains be allowed free circulation for the people."
translations.idiomatic: Fujian lies beyond the mountains; the people there should be allowed to use old coin freely."

sentences.zh: 上韙其言，盡寬舊錢廢錢之禁。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his words and fully relaxed the ban on old and demonetized coins.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved, and restrictions on old and demonetized coin were broadly relaxed.

sentences.zh: 是年定旗籍私鑄私銷罪如律。

translations.literal: That year penalties for Banner people who privately cast or melted were fixed according to statute.
translations.idiomatic: That year Banner subjects who privately minted or melted were made subject to the same penalties as commoners.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，以循舊制改輕錢，私鑄復起，廷臣請罷小制錢，仍鑄一錢四分重錢，新舊錢暫兼行，新錢千准銀一兩，舊錢准七錢。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year, reverting to the old standard changed to light coins; private casting revived; court ministers requested abolishing small-denomination coins and again casting one-mace-four-fen heavy coins; new and old coins temporarily circulated together; new coins at one thousand per tael of silver, old at seven hundred cash.
translations.idiomatic: In year 41 a return to the lighter standard revived private minting. Ministers asked to abolish small coin and restore the one-mace-four-fen standard, with old and new circulating together at 1000 new or 700 old cash per tael of silver.

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved.

sentences.zh: 然私鑄竟不能止。

translations.literal: Yet private casting could not be stopped after all.
translations.idiomatic: Private minting nevertheless could not be stopped.

sentences.zh: 四十五年，山東請鑄大錢。

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year Shandong requested casting large coins.
translations.idiomatic: In year 45 Shandong petitioned to cast large-denomination coins.

sentences.zh: 會獲得常山私鑄，上以私鑄不盡大錢，必多私銷，宜先收後禁，乃令錢糧銀一兩折收二千文，錢盡，折收銅器。

translations.literal: When private casting was discovered at Changshan, the emperor said that if private casting did not end with large coins, there would be much private melting; it was better to collect first and ban later; therefore grain-tax silver was ordered collected at two thousand cash per tael; when cash was exhausted, copper vessels were accepted in payment.
translations.idiomatic: When a private mint was uncovered at Changshan, the emperor reasoned that large coins would only encourage more illicit melting unless copper were collected first. Grain tax was henceforth collected at 2000 cash per tael of silver, then in copperware once cash ran out.

sentences.zh: 戶部以新錢不敷，請展至五年後毀舊鑄。

translations.literal: The Board of Revenue, because new coins were insufficient, requested extending destruction of old coin and recasting to five years later.
translations.idiomatic: The Board of Revenue, finding new coin insufficient, asked to postpone withdrawal of old coin for five years.

sentences.zh: 越二年，襄陽私鑄錢潛貯漕艘入京，大理卿塔進泰奉命會查，疏請嚴禁收毀，再犯私鑄私販罪如律，船戶運弁罪同私鑄，地方官知情，斬決，沒其家；

translations.literal: Two years later, privately cast cash from Xiangyang was secretly stored on grain-transport ships entering the capital; Chief Minister of Justice Ta Jintai was ordered to investigate jointly; he memorialized requesting strict prohibition and collection for destruction; repeat offenders in private casting and trafficking were punished by statute; boatmen and transport officers were punished as private casters; local officials who knew were decapitated and their families confiscated;
translations.idiomatic: Two years later, privately minted Xiangyang coin was found hidden aboard grain boats bound for the capital. Chief Minister Ta Jintai investigated and memorialized for stricter collection and destruction. Repeat offenders in minting and trafficking were punished by statute; boatmen and transport officers were treated as minters; knowing local officials were beheaded and their families confiscated;

sentences.zh: 失察，奪職。

translations.literal: failure to detect led to dismissal from office.
translations.idiomatic: failure to detect led to dismissal.

sentences.zh: 法益加嚴。

translations.literal: The law grew stricter still.
translations.idiomatic: Penalties grew still harsher.

sentences.zh: 官局用銅，自四十四年兼采滇產。

translations.literal: Copper for official bureaus, from the forty-fourth year, was partly sourced from Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: From year 44 official mints partly drew copper from Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，巡撫楊名時請歲運滇銅入京。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng, Governor Yang Mingshi requested annual transport of Yunnan copper to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 1 Governor Yang Mingshi petitioned for annual shipment of Yunnan copper to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 廷議即山鑄錢為便，因開雲南大理、霑益四局，鑄運京錢，幕文曰「雲泉」。

translations.literal: The court debated that casting on site was more convenient; therefore four bureaus were opened at Dali and Zhan Yi in Yunnan to cast coin for transport to the capital, with reverse inscription "Yunquan."
translations.idiomatic: The court decided that minting locally was cheaper. Four Yunnan mints were opened at Dali and Zhan Yi to cast coin for shipment to the capital, inscribed yunquan on the reverse.

sentences.zh: 上以錢為國寶，更名「寶雲」，並令直省局錢，幕首「寶」字，次省名，純滿文。

translations.literal: The emperor, holding coin as a national treasure, renamed it "Baoyun," and ordered provincial bureau coins to bear first the character "bao," then the province name, all in Manchu script.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, treating coin as a national treasure, renamed the mint Baoyun and ordered all provincial coins to show bao followed by the province name in Manchu script alone.

sentences.zh: 其後運京錢時鑄時罷。

translations.literal: Thereafter coin for transport to the capital was sometimes cast and sometimes suspended.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter coin minted for shipment to the capital was intermittently suspended.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二年，以錢價久不平，飭大興、宛平置錢行官牙以平錢價。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianlong, because the price of cash had long been unsettled, Daxing and Wanping were ordered to establish official money brokers to level the price.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 2, because the cash rate had long been unstable, Daxing and Wanping counties were ordered to set up official money brokers to stabilize it.

sentences.zh: 上念私銷害尤甚，益厲行銅器禁。

translations.literal: The emperor, mindful that private melting was especially harmful, enforced the ban on copper vessels more strictly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor judged illicit melting the greater evil and tightened the ban on copperware.

sentences.zh: 官非三品以上不聽用，舊有銅器限三年內輸官，逾限以私藏禁物論，已禁仍造，罪比盜鑄為從。

translations.literal: Officials below third rank were not permitted to use them; existing copper vessels had to be surrendered within three years; after the deadline possession was treated as hoarding forbidden goods; if still manufactured after the ban, punishment equaled accomplice in illicit casting.
translations.idiomatic: Officials below third rank were forbidden copperware; existing pieces had to be surrendered within three years, after which possession was a crime; continued manufacture after the ban was punished as complicity in illicit minting.

sentences.zh: 遂通令禁造銅器。

translations.literal: Thus a general order forbade manufacture of copper vessels.
translations.idiomatic: A general ban on copperware manufacture followed.

sentences.zh: 尋益嚴限制，惟一品始聽用，餘悉禁之，藏匿私用，皆以違禁論。

translations.literal: Soon restrictions grew stricter: only first rank was permitted use; all others were forbidden; concealment and private use were all treated as violation of prohibition.
translations.idiomatic: Restrictions soon tightened further: only first-rank officials might keep copperware; all others were forbidden, and concealment was a punishable offense.

sentences.zh: 十二年，上以錢重則私銷，輕則私鑄，令復一錢二分舊制。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year the emperor said heavy coins invite private melting, light coins invite private casting, and ordered restoration of the old one-mace-two-fen standard.
translations.idiomatic: In year 12 the emperor observed that heavy coin encouraged melting and light coin encouraged counterfeiting, and restored the one-mace-two-fen standard.

sentences.zh: 十三年，定翦錢邊律罪為絞監候。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, the statutory penalty for clipping coin edges was fixed as strangulation after reprieve.
translations.idiomatic: In year 13 clipping coin edges was made a capital offense with reprieve (jiao jianhou).

sentences.zh: 先是尚書海望以銅禁病民，疏陳四弊，高宗然之，遂罷禁銅收銅令。

translations.literal: Earlier Minister Haiwang, because the copper ban harmed the people, memorialized listing four abuses; Gaozong agreed and abolished the bans on copper and collection of copper.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Minister Haiwang had memorialized that the copper ban harmed the people in four ways; Qianlong agreed and lifted both the copper ban and compulsory copper collection.

sentences.zh: 復以京師錢價昂，銀一兩僅易八百文，詔發工部節慎庫錢平價。

translations.literal: Again because cash in the capital was dear, one tael of silver exchanged for only eight hundred cash; an edict released coin from the Board of Works Jieshen treasury to level the price.
translations.idiomatic: Cash in the capital rose again to only 800 per tael of silver; an edict released Board of Works treasury coin to stabilize the rate.

sentences.zh: 御史陶正靖疏陳錢價不平，弊由經紀蠹害錢法，遽命革除之。

translations.literal: Censor Tao Zhengjing memorialized that the unsettled price of cash stemmed from brokers who harmed the coinage system; he was immediately ordered to abolish them.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Tao Zhengjing blamed brokers for distorting the cash rate; they were immediately abolished.

sentences.zh: 浙江布政使張若震言錢貴弊在私毀。

translations.literal: Zhejiang Provincial Administration Commissioner Zhang Ruozhen said the harm of dear cash lay in private destruction.
translations.idiomatic: Zhejiang Commissioner Zhang Ruozhen argued that dear cash was caused by illicit destruction.

sentences.zh: 如使配合銅鉛，參入點錫，鑄成青錢，則銷者無利。

translations.literal: If copper and lead were alloyed with a touch of tin to cast green cash, melters would gain no profit.
translations.idiomatic: If coins were alloyed with copper, lead, and a trace of tin to produce green cash, melters would find no profit in destroying them.

sentences.zh: 試之驗，因采其議，鑄與黃錢兼行。

translations.literal: Trials proved successful; his proposal was adopted, and green cash was cast to circulate with yellow cash.
translations.idiomatic: Trials succeeded; his proposal was adopted, and green cash circulated alongside yellow cash.

sentences.zh: 定私鑄鉛錢禁，為首及匠人絞監候，為從及知情買使，減一等。

translations.literal: The ban on private casting of lead cash was fixed: ringleaders and craftsmen, strangulation after reprieve; accomplices and knowing purchasers, one degree lighter.
translations.idiomatic: Penalties for private lead coin were set: ringleaders and craftsmen received strangulation with reprieve; accomplices and knowing buyers one degree less.

sentences.zh: 申嚴販運及囤積制錢之禁，凡積錢至百千以上，以違例論。

translations.literal: The ban on trafficking and hoarding of demonetized coins was strictly renewed; anyone hoarding above one hundred strings was prosecuted as violation of regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Trafficking and hoarding of demonetized coin were strictly forbidden; hoarding above one hundred strings was a regulatory offense.

sentences.zh: 上諭廷臣曰：「今之言禁者，亦第補偏救弊，非能正本清源也。

translations.literal: The emperor instructed the court: "Those who speak of prohibition today only patch partial abuses and rescue symptoms; they cannot rectify the root and clear the source."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told the court: "Today's prohibitions only patch symptoms; they do not address the root cause."

sentences.zh: 物之定直以銀不以錢，而官民乃皆便錢不便銀，趨利之徒，以使低昂為得計，何輕重之倒置也？

translations.literal: The fixed value of goods is in silver, not cash, yet officials and people all find cash convenient and silver inconvenient; profit-seekers take manipulating high and low as their strategy—how inverted are heavy and light!
translations.idiomatic: Goods are properly valued in silver, not cash, yet officials and commoners alike prefer cash to silver. Profiteers manipulate the rate for gain—how inverted are the true and false standards of value!

sentences.zh: 嗣是宜重用銀，凡直省官修工程，民間總置貨物，皆以銀。

translations.literal: Henceforth silver should be heavily used; all provincial official construction projects and private bulk purchases of goods should be in silver."
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth silver should be emphasized: all provincial public works and large private purchases should be settled in silver."

sentences.zh: 二十二年，兩廣總督李侍堯請禁舊錢、偽錢。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, Governor-General of Liangguang Li Shiyao requested banning old and counterfeit coins.
translations.idiomatic: In year 22 Liangguang Governor-General Li Shiyao petitioned to ban old and counterfeit coin.

sentences.zh: 上以民間雜用吳三桂「利用」、「洪化」、「昭武」諸偽錢，第聽自檢出，官為易之以充鑄，舊錢仍聽行使。

translations.literal: The emperor said that among the people Wu Sangui's counterfeit coins Liyong, Honghua, and Zhaowu were mixed in use; they need only be voluntarily surrendered; the government would exchange them for recasting; old coins were still permitted to circulate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor noted that Wu Sangui's Liyong, Honghua, and Zhaowu counterfeits circulated among the people; voluntary surrender would be exchanged for official coin to be recast, while old coin might still circulate.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，回部平，頒式於葉爾羌，鑄「乾隆通寶」，枚重二錢，幕鑄葉爾羌名，左滿文，右迴文，用紅銅，並毀舊普爾錢充鑄。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, when the Muslim regions were pacified, the standard was promulgated at Yarkand; Qianlong Tongbao was cast, each weighing two mace, reverse bearing the Yarkand name, Manchu script left, Uighur script right, using red copper, and old Pul coins were destroyed for recasting.
translations.idiomatic: In year 24, after the Muslim regions were pacified, the standard was issued at Yarkand: Qianlong Tongbao of two mace, reverse with the Yarkand name in Manchu on the left and Uighur on the right, cast in red copper from melted old Pul coin.

sentences.zh: 越二年，阿克蘇請鑄，如葉爾羌例。

translations.literal: Two years later Aksu requested casting, following the Yarkand precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later Aksu petitioned to mint on the Yarkand model.

sentences.zh: 復允西藏開鑄銀錢，重一錢與五分二種，文曰「乾隆寶藏」，幕用唐古忒字，邊郭識年分。

translations.literal: Tibet was also permitted to cast silver coins in two weights of one mace and five fen, inscribed Qianlong Baozang, reverse in Tangut script, rim bearing the year.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet was also permitted to mint silver coins of one mace and five fen, inscribed Qianlong Baozang, with Tangut script on the reverse and the year on the rim.

sentences.zh: 以上二類錢，第行之回、藏，內地不用。

translations.literal: The above two types of coin circulated only in the Muslim regions and Tibet; the interior did not use them.
translations.idiomatic: These two types circulated only in the Muslim west and Tibet, not in China proper.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，令回部鑄錢，永用乾隆年號。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, the Muslim regions were ordered to cast coin permanently using the Qianlong reign title.
translations.idiomatic: In year 29 the Muslim regions were ordered to use the Qianlong reign title permanently on their coinage.

sentences.zh: 時至中葉，錢直昂，直省皆增爐廣鑄，價暫趨於平。

translations.literal: By mid-dynasty cash was dear; all provinces increased furnaces and expanded casting; the price temporarily approached equilibrium.
translations.idiomatic: By mid-dynasty cash was dear; provinces added furnaces and increased output, and the rate briefly stabilized.

sentences.zh: 會銅運遲滯，市儈居奇增直，害錢法，通飭督撫毋得輕請停爐減卯。

translations.literal: When copper transport lagged, market speculators hoarded to raise prices, harming the coinage system; governors-general and governors were generally ordered not to lightly request stopping furnaces or reducing mao.
translations.idiomatic: When copper shipments lagged, speculators hoarded and raised prices, harming the currency. Governors were ordered not to suspend mints or cut production cycles without strong cause.

sentences.zh: 季年私鑄益多，四川、雲、貴為淵藪，流布及江、浙。

translations.literal: In the late years private casting increased; Sichuan, Yunnan, and Guizhou were their lair, spreading to Jiangsu and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: By the late reign private minting flourished, centered in Sichuan, Yunnan, and Guizhou and spreading to the lower Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 雲、貴官錢亦以不善罷鑄。

translations.literal: Official coin of Yunnan and Guizhou was also suspended for poor quality.
translations.idiomatic: Official minting in Yunnan and Guizhou was also suspended for poor quality.

sentences.zh: 又自律嚴私鑄，常寬之以收毀，莠民恃以行詐，私錢日出不窮。

translations.literal: Again, though prohibition of private casting was strict, leniency in collection and destruction was common; wicked men relied on this to commit fraud, and private coins issued daily without end.
translations.idiomatic: Although private minting was strictly forbidden, lenient collection policies let criminals exploit the gap, and counterfeit coin proliferated daily.

sentences.zh: 五十七年，湖廣總督畢沅請收買毋立限。

translations.literal: In the fifty-seventh year Huguang Governor-General Bi Yuan requested purchase without setting a deadline.
translations.idiomatic: In year 57 Huguang Governor-General Bi Yuan petitioned for open-ended purchase of private coin.

sentences.zh: 上謂湖北乃私鑄總匯，不圖禁絕而預思所以卸過，命嚴稽私販，仍予寬限二年。

translations.literal: The emperor said Hubei was the chief depot of private casting; instead of planning to stop it, he was already thinking how to shift blame; he ordered strict inspection of private trafficking, still granting a two-year grace period.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied that Hubei was the main conduit for private coin and that Bi was planning evasion rather than suppression; he ordered strict inspection of trafficking but granted a two-year grace period.

sentences.zh: 五十九年，以官私錢錯出，錢賤，乃暫罷直省鑄，私錢通限一年收繳，而吏胥緣為奸。

translations.literal: In the fifty-ninth year, because official and private coins were confused in circulation and cash was cheap, provincial minting was temporarily suspended; private coins were generally limited to one year for collection; yet clerks and runners used this as pretext for corruption.
translations.idiomatic: In year 59 official and private coin became indistinguishable and cash depreciated; provincial minting was suspended and private coin ordered collected within one year—but clerks exploited the policy for graft.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶元年，復直省鑄。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiaqing, provincial minting was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 1 provincial minting resumed.

sentences.zh: 至十年，直省未盡復卯，錢復貴，通飭各督撫按卯鼓鑄。

translations.literal: By the tenth year provinces had not fully restored mao production; cash was dear again; all governors-general and governors were ordered to cast by the full mao quota.
translations.idiomatic: By year 10 many provinces had not restored full production cycles; cash rose again, and all governors were ordered to meet their minting quotas.

sentences.zh: 然嗣是局私私鑄相踵起，京局錢至輪郭肉好糢糊脆薄，「寶蘇」鑄中雜沙子，擲地即碎，而貴州、湖廣私鑄盛行，江蘇官局私局秘匿。

translations.literal: Yet thereafter official and private casting rose in succession; capital mint coins had rims, flesh, and good metal blurred, brittle and thin; Baosu coins mixed in sand and shattered when thrown to the ground; while Guizhou and Huguang private casting flourished, and Jiangsu official and private bureaus concealed their operations.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter official and private minting alike deteriorated: Beijing coin had blurred rims and thin, brittle metal; Jiangsu Baosu coin mixed in sand and shattered when dropped; private minting flourished in Guizhou and Huguang while Jiangsu hid both official and illicit operations.

sentences.zh: 至道光間，閩、廣雜行「光中」、「景中」、「景興」、「嘉隆」諸夷錢，奸民利之，輒從仿造。

translations.literal: By the Daoguang period, Fujian and Guangdong mixed in circulation various foreign coins Guangzhong, Jingzhong, Jingxing, and Jialong; wicked men profited and constantly imitated them.
translations.idiomatic: By the Daoguang era Fujian and Guangdong circulated foreign coins such as Guangzhong, Jingzhong, Jingxing, and Jialong; criminals profited by imitating them.

sentences.zh: 貴陽大定官局亦別鑄底大錢，錢法自是益壞。

translations.literal: The official bureaus at Guiyang and Dading also separately cast large coins with thick bases; the coinage system from then grew worse.
translations.idiomatic: The Guiyang and Dading mints also cast thick-based large coins, and the currency deteriorated further.

sentences.zh: 時華洋互市，以貨易銀，番船冒禁，歲漏出以千萬計，御史黃中模、章沅咸以為言。

translations.literal: At the time China and the West traded goods for silver; foreign ships evaded prohibition, leaking out tens of millions yearly; Censors Huang Zhongmo and Zhang Yuan all reported this.
translations.idiomatic: As Sino-Western trade exchanged goods for silver, foreign ships smuggled out tens of millions of taels annually; Censors Huang Zhongmo and Zhang Yuan both memorialized on the matter.

sentences.zh: 而大髻、小髻、蓬頭、蝙蝠、雙柱、馬劍各種番銀，亦潛輸內地以規利，自閩、廣通行至黃河以南。

translations.literal: Moreover various foreign silvers—large queue, small queue, disheveled head, bat, double pillar, and horse sword—were also secretly brought into the interior for profit, circulating from Fujian and Guangdong south of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: Various foreign silver dollars—large and small queue, disheveled head, bat, double pillar, and horse sword types—were also smuggled inland for profit, spreading from Fujian and Guangdong to all regions south of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 而洋商復挾至各省海口，陽置貨而陰市銀，至洋銀日多，紋銀日少而貴。

translations.literal: Foreign merchants also brought them to every provincial seaport, ostensibly selling goods but secretly buying silver, until foreign silver grew daily and sycee grew scarce and dear.
translations.idiomatic: Foreign merchants also carried them to every coastal port, ostensibly trading goods but secretly buying silver, until foreign dollars proliferated and sycee grew scarce and costly.

sentences.zh: 上患之，命粵督申嚴禁約，然所禁不及洋銀，仿鑄之廣板、福板、杭板、吳庄、行庄，耗華銀如故。

translations.literal: The emperor was troubled and ordered the Guangdong governor to renew strict prohibitions, yet what was forbidden did not include foreign silver; imitations such as Guangban, Fuban, Hangban, Wuzhuang, and Xingzhuang continued to drain Chinese silver as before.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was alarmed and ordered the Guangdong governor to tighten enforcement, but foreign silver was not banned; counterfeit Guangban, Fuban, Hangban, Wuzhuang, and Xingzhuang types continued to drain domestic silver as before.

sentences.zh: 御史黃爵滋請並禁使出洋，更立專條，議從重科。

translations.literal: Censor Huang Juezi requested also forbidding export overseas and establishing a separate statute; heavier penalties were debated.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Huang Juezi petitioned to ban silver export entirely and establish a separate statute with heavier penalties.

sentences.zh: 十七年，詔沿江沿海督撫、海關監督，飭屬嚴稽偷漏，定功過，行賞罰，而海內銀卒耗竭，每兩易錢常至二千。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year an edict ordered governors along the rivers and coast and customs superintendents to strictly inspect smuggling, fix merit and demerit, and enforce rewards and punishments; yet silver within the seas was finally exhausted, and one tael often exchanged for two thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: In year 17 an edict ordered coastal governors and customs officials to crack down on smuggling with merit-based rewards and punishments, but domestic silver was exhausted and one tael often bought only 2000 cash.

sentences.zh: 廷臣謀所以重錢以殺銀之勢，而議格不行。

translations.literal: Court ministers plotted how to strengthen cash to curb silver's dominance, but the proposal was blocked and not implemented.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers debated strengthening cash to curb silver, but the proposal never took effect.

sentences.zh: 先是道光中葉，銀外泄而貴，朝野皆欲行大錢以救之。

translations.literal: Earlier in mid-Daoguang, silver leaked abroad and grew dear; court and populace all wished to issue large coins to remedy it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier in mid-Daoguang, as silver drained abroad and rose in value, both court and public favored issuing large-denomination coins as a remedy.

sentences.zh: 廣西巡撫梁章鉅疏言其利。

translations.literal: Guangxi Governor Liang Zhangju memorialized on its benefits.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxi Governor Liang Zhangju memorialized in favor of the policy.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，四川學政何紹基力請行大錢以復古救時。

translations.literal: When Wenzong ascended the throne, Sichuan Education Commissioner He Shaoji strongly petitioned to issue large coins to restore antiquity and rescue the times.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianfeng ascended the throne, Sichuan Education Commissioner He Shaoji strongly urged large coins to restore ancient practice and save the currency.

sentences.zh: 上意初不謂然，卒與官票、寶鈔行焉。

translations.literal: The emperor at first did not agree, but in the end official notes and treasure notes were issued together.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was initially unconvinced but eventually authorized official notes and treasure notes alongside large coins.

sentences.zh: 鈔嘗行於順治八年，歲造十二萬八千有奇。

translations.literal: Paper notes had been issued in Shunzhi year 8, with annual production of a little over 128,000.
translations.idiomatic: Paper notes had been issued in Shunzhi 8, with annual production exceeding 128,000.

sentences.zh: 十年而罷。

translations.literal: After ten years they were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: They were abolished after ten years.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶間，侍講學士蔡之定請行鈔。

translations.literal: During Jiaqing, Hanlin Bachelor Cai Zhiding requested issuing notes.
translations.idiomatic: During Jiaqing, Hanlin Bachelor Cai Zhiding petitioned to issue paper notes.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年，福建巡撫王懿德亦以為請。

translations.literal: In Xianfeng year 2, Fujian Governor Wang Yide also petitioned likewise.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 2 Fujian Governor Wang Yide made the same request.

sentences.zh: 廷議以窒礙難行，卻之。

translations.literal: The court debated that obstacles made it impracticable and rejected it.
translations.idiomatic: The court judged it impracticable and rejected both petitions.

sentences.zh: 是時銀虧錢匱重，而軍需河餉糜帑二千數百萬，籌國計者，率以行官票請。

translations.literal: At the time silver was scarce and cash exhausted; military supplies and river conservancy consumed over twenty million from the treasury; those planning state finance mostly petitioned to issue official notes.
translations.idiomatic: Silver was scarce, cash exhausted, and military and river works consumed over twenty million taels; fiscal planners overwhelmingly urged official notes.

sentences.zh: 次年，命戶部集議。

translations.literal: The next year the Board of Revenue was ordered to convene deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the Board of Revenue was ordered to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 惠親等請飭部製造錢鈔與銀票相輔並行。

translations.literal: Prince Hui and others requested ordering the ministry to manufacture cash notes to circulate alongside silver notes in mutual support.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Hui and others urged the ministry to issue cash notes alongside silver notes.

sentences.zh: 票鈔制以皮紙，額題「戶部官票」，左滿、右漢，皆雙行，中標二兩平足色銀若干兩，下曰「戶部奏行官票」。

translations.literal: Notes were made of parchment paper, titled at the top "Board of Revenue Official Note," Manchu left and Han right, both in double columns; the center marked standard sycee of two taels in such-and-such amount; below read "Official Note Issued by Memorial of the Board of Revenue."
translations.idiomatic: Notes were printed on parchment, headed "Board of Revenue Official Note" in Manchu on the left and Han on the right; the center stated the amount in standard sycee of two taels; the footer read "Official Note Issued by Memorial of the Board of Revenue."

sentences.zh: 凡原將官票兌換銀錢者，與銀一律，並准按部定章程，搭交官項。

translations.literal: All who originally exchanged official notes for silver or cash were treated the same as silver, and permitted to pay official dues according to ministry regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Official notes were redeemable for silver or cash on the same terms as silver itself and could be used for official payments per ministry regulations.

sentences.zh: 偽造者依律治罪。

translations.literal: Counterfeiters were punished according to statute.
translations.idiomatic: Counterfeiting was punishable by statute.

sentences.zh: 邊文龍。

translations.literal: Border text: dragon.
translations.idiomatic: The border bore a dragon design.

sentences.zh: 鈔額題「大清寶鈔」，漢字平列，中標準足制錢若干文，旁八字為「天下通寶，平準出入」，下曰「此鈔即代制錢行用，並准按成交納地丁錢糧一切稅課捐項，京、外各庫一概收解」。

translations.literal: The note was titled "Great Qing Treasure Note," Han characters in parallel columns; the center marked standard regulated cash in such-and-such wen; at the side eight characters read "Treasure circulating under Heaven, balanced in and out"; below read "This note substitutes for regulated cash in circulation and may be used for land tax, grain tax, and all levies and contributions; all treasuries capital and provincial shall receive and remit it."
translations.idiomatic: Treasure notes were headed "Great Qing Treasure Note"; the center stated the amount in standard cash; the margin bore eight characters: "Treasure circulating under Heaven, balanced in and out"; the footer declared that the note substituted for regulated cash and was acceptable for land tax, grain tax, and all levies at every treasury.

sentences.zh: 邊文如票。

translations.literal: Border text as on the note.
translations.idiomatic: The border design matched that on the official note.

sentences.zh: 大錢當千至當十，凡五等，重自二兩遞減至四錢四分。

translations.literal: Large coins ranged from denomination 1000 to denomination 10, five grades in all, weight decreasing from two taels to four mace four fen.
translations.idiomatic: Large coins ranged from 1000-cash to 10-cash denominations in five grades, weight decreasing from two taels to four mace four fen.

sentences.zh: 當千、當五百，淨銅鑄造，色紫；

translations.literal: Denominations 1000 and 500 were cast in pure copper, purple in color;
translations.idiomatic: The 1000- and 500-cash denominations were cast in pure copper with a purple tint;

sentences.zh: 當百、當五十、當十，銅鉛配鑄，色黃。

translations.literal: denominations 100, 50, and 10 were alloyed copper and lead, yellow in color.
translations.idiomatic: the 100-, 50-, and 10-cash denominations were cast from copper-lead alloy with a yellow tint.

sentences.zh: 百以上文曰「咸豐元寶」，以下曰「重寶」，幕滿文局名。

translations.literal: Above denomination 100 the inscription read "Xianfeng Yuanbao"; below read "Zhongbao"; reverse bore the mint name in Manchu.
translations.idiomatic: Coins of 100 cash and above were inscribed Xianfeng Yuanbao; lower denominations read Zhongbao; the reverse bore the mint name in Manchu.

sentences.zh: 四年，以乏銅，兼鑄當五鐵錢及制錢。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, for lack of copper, denomination-5 iron coins and regulated cash were also cast.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4, for lack of copper, 5-cash iron coins and standard cash were also minted.

sentences.zh: 已而更鑄鉛制錢。

translations.literal: Later regulated cash of lead was also cast.
translations.idiomatic: Lead standard cash was added later.

sentences.zh: 乾隆間，京局用銅，滇、洋兼資，後專行滇運。

translations.literal: During Qianlong, capital mints used copper from both Yunnan and foreign sources; later only Yunnan transport was used.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qianlong the capital mints drew on Yunnan and imported copper; later only Yunnan shipments were used.

sentences.zh: 時以道梗銅滯，故權宜出此。

translations.literal: At the time routes were blocked and copper delayed, so this expedient was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Blocked transport routes delayed copper shipments, making these expedients necessary.

sentences.zh: 定議票銀一兩抵制錢二千，鈔二千抵銀一兩，票鈔亦準是互相抵，民間完納丁糧稅課及一切官款，亦准五成，京、外應放庫款如之。

translations.literal: It was decided that one tael of note silver equaled two thousand cash, two thousand in notes equaled one tael of silver, notes and cash notes likewise offset each other; popular payment of land tax, grain tax, and all official dues was also permitted at fifty percent; capital and provincial treasury disbursements followed the same rule.
translations.idiomatic: One tael of note silver equaled 2000 cash; 2000 in notes equaled one tael of silver; notes and cash notes were mutually convertible. Private tax payments and all official dues could be paid half in notes; treasury disbursements followed the same rule.

sentences.zh: 大錢上下通行如票鈔，抵銀如制錢之數，輸官以三成，鐵錢通用如大錢。

translations.literal: Large coins circulated at all levels like notes; they offset silver at the rate of regulated cash; thirty percent was accepted for official payment; iron coins circulated like large coins.
translations.idiomatic: Large coins circulated like notes at the standard cash rate; thirty percent of official payments could be in large coins; iron coins circulated on the same terms.

sentences.zh: 阻撓罪以違制，偽造鈔票斬監候，私鑄加嚴。

translations.literal: Obstruction was punished as violation of regulations; counterfeiting notes was decapitation after reprieve; private casting was tightened.
translations.idiomatic: Obstruction was a regulatory offense; counterfeiting notes carried the death penalty with reprieve; private minting penalties were tightened.

sentences.zh: 通飭京、外設置官錢局。

translations.literal: A general order directed capital and provinces to establish official money bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: Capital and provinces were ordered to establish official money bureaus.

sentences.zh: 尋以直省延不奉行，嗣後議於各府置鈔局，發大錢於行店，俾錢鈔通融互易以便民，丁糧搭收票鈔，零星小戶銀鈔尾零，搭交銅鐵大錢，皆先從直隸、山東實行。

translations.literal: Soon because provinces delayed compliance, it was later debated to place note bureaus in each prefecture, distribute large coins to shops so cash and notes could be exchanged for popular convenience; land tax accepted notes; small households with fractional silver or note remainders paid in copper and iron large coins—all first implemented in Zhili and Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: When provinces delayed compliance, note bureaus were proposed for each prefecture and large coins distributed to shops for exchange. Land tax accepted notes; small taxpayers with fractional balances paid in copper and iron large coins—Zhili and Shandong implemented first.

sentences.zh: 官吏折勒骫法，商民交易不平價，從嚴處治。

translations.literal: Officials who extorted or bent the law, and merchants who traded at unfair prices, were severely punished.
translations.idiomatic: Official extortion and unfair trading were severely punished.

sentences.zh: 七年，令順天直隸各屬錢糧，自本年上忙始，以實銀四成、寶鈔三成、當十銅鐵大錢三成搭交，一切用項，亦按成搭放。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, grain tax in Shuntian and Zhili subordinates from the first busy season of the year was ordered paid forty percent in real silver, thirty percent in treasure notes, thirty percent in denomination-10 copper and iron large coins; all expenditures were disbursed in the same proportions.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 Zhili grain tax from the first harvest season was payable forty percent in silver, thirty percent in treasure notes, and thirty percent in 10-cash copper and iron large coins; all official payments followed the same ratio.

sentences.zh: 尋從戶部議，自本年下忙始，直隸照銀七票三徵收，大錢三成即納在鈔票三成內，交票交錢聽便。

translations.literal: Soon following Board of Revenue deliberation, from the second busy season Zhili collected at seventy percent silver and thirty percent notes; the thirty percent in large coins was included within the thirty percent in notes and cash notes; payment in notes or cash was at the payer's choice.
translations.idiomatic: Following Board deliberation, from the second harvest season Zhili collected seventy percent silver and thirty percent notes, with large coins counted within the thirty-percent note quota; payers could choose notes or cash.

sentences.zh: 然鈔法初行，始而軍餉，繼而河工，搭放皆稱不便，民情疑阻。

translations.literal: Yet when the note system first operated, first military pay, then river works—all disbursements in notes were called inconvenient, and popular sentiment was doubtful and obstructive.
translations.idiomatic: When notes were first issued, military pay and river works disbursements in notes were widely resisted, and public confidence was low.

sentences.zh: 直省搭收五成，以款多抵撥既艱，搭放遂不復肯搭收。

translations.literal: Provinces accepting fifty percent in notes, because large sums made offsetting difficult, ceased willing to accept notes in disbursement.
translations.idiomatic: Provinces that accepted fifty percent in notes found large-sum settlement difficult and stopped accepting notes in disbursement.

sentences.zh: 民間得鈔，積為無用，京師持鈔入市，非故增直，即匿貨，持向官號商鋪，所得皆四項大錢，不便用，故鈔行而中外兵民病之。

translations.literal: When the people obtained notes they hoarded them as useless; in the capital those bringing notes to market either had prices deliberately raised or goods hidden; at official shops and stores what they received were all four types of large coins, inconvenient to use—thus when notes circulated, soldiers and civilians within and without all suffered.
translations.idiomatic: The public hoarded notes as worthless. In the capital, note-holders faced inflated prices or hidden goods; official shops paid out only the four large-coin types, which were hard to use. Notes thus harmed soldiers and civilians alike.

sentences.zh: 其後京師以官號七折錢發鈔，直益低落，至減發亦窮應付，鈔遂不能行矣。

translations.literal: Later the capital issued notes through official shops at seventy percent of cash value; the price fell further; even reduced issuance could barely meet demand; notes could no longer circulate.
translations.idiomatic: Later Beijing shops issued notes at seventy percent of face value; the rate fell further until even reduced issuance could not meet demand, and notes ceased to circulate.

sentences.zh: 大錢當千、當五百，以折當過重最先廢，當百、當五十繼廢，鐵錢以私票梗之而亦廢，乃專行當十錢。

translations.literal: Large coins of denominations 1000 and 500, because their exchange value was too heavy, were abolished first; denominations 100 and 50 followed; iron coins were blocked by private notes and also abolished; only denomination-10 coins remained.
translations.idiomatic: The 1000- and 500-cash large coins were abolished first as overvalued; the 100- and 50-cash followed; iron coins were driven out by private notes; only the 10-cash denomination remained.

sentences.zh: 盜鑄叢起，死罪日報而不為止。

translations.literal: Illicit casting rose in clusters; death sentences were reported daily yet did not stop it.
translations.idiomatic: Counterfeiting proliferated despite daily death sentences.

sentences.zh: 局錢亦漸惡，雜私鑄中不復辨，奸商因之折減挑剔，任意低昂。

translations.literal: Mint coins also gradually worsened, mixed with private casting beyond distinction; unscrupulous merchants therefore discounted and picked flaws, arbitrarily raising or lowering prices.
translations.idiomatic: Official coin deteriorated until it was indistinguishable from counterfeits; merchants exploited the confusion with arbitrary discounts.

sentences.zh: 商販患得大錢，皆裹足，三成搭收，徒張文告，屢禁罔效。

translations.literal: Merchants dreaded obtaining large coins and all held back; the thirty-percent acceptance rule was only empty proclamations; repeated prohibitions had no effect.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants refused large coins; the thirty-percent acceptance rule remained on paper only, and repeated prohibitions failed.

sentences.zh: 法弊而撓法者多，固未有濟也。

translations.literal: The law was debased and those who thwarted the law were many; naturally nothing was achieved.
translations.idiomatic: The law was broken and widely evaded; nothing was achieved.

sentences.zh: 當十錢行獨久，然一錢當制錢二，出國門即不通行。

translations.literal: Denomination-10 coins alone circulated long, yet one mace equaled two regulated cash; outside the capital gates they did not circulate.
translations.idiomatic: Only the 10-cash coin circulated for long, worth two standard cash per mace, but it did not circulate outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 咸豐之季，銅苦乏，申禁銅、收銅令。

translations.literal: In the late Xianfeng period copper was painfully scarce; bans on copper and orders to collect copper were renewed.
translations.idiomatic: In late Xianfeng copper was desperately scarce, and copper bans and collection orders were renewed.

sentences.zh: 同治初，鑄錢所資，惟商銅、廢銅，當十錢減從三錢二分。

translations.literal: In early Tongzhi, resources for casting were only merchant copper and scrap copper; denomination-10 coins were reduced to three mace two fen.
translations.idiomatic: In early Tongzhi minting relied only on merchant and scrap copper; the 10-cash coin was reduced to three mace two fen.

sentences.zh: 光緒九年，復減為二錢六分。

translations.literal: In Guangxu year 9 it was again reduced to two mace six fen.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 9 it was further reduced to two mace six fen.

sentences.zh: 時孝欽顯皇后銳意欲復製，下廷臣議，以滇銅運不如額，姑市洋銅，交機器局試鑄。

translations.literal: At the time Empress Dowager Cixi was keen to restore casting; court ministers were ordered to deliberate; because Yunnan copper transport fell short of quota, foreign copper was temporarily purchased and trial casting entrusted to the machine bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Cixi was determined to restore standard coinage. With Yunnan copper shipments below quota, foreign copper was purchased for trial minting at the machine bureau.

sentences.zh: 戶部奏稱機器局鑄錢並京局開爐之不便，懿旨罪其委卸，卒命直隸總督李鴻章於天津行之，重准一錢，遂賞唐炯巡撫銜，專督雲南銅政。

translations.literal: The Board of Revenue memorialized that machine-bureau casting and reopening capital furnaces were inconvenient; an imperial rescript blamed their shirking; finally Zhili Governor-General Li Hongzhang was ordered to implement it at Tianjin at one mace weight; Tang Jiong was granted the rank of governor and specially supervised Yunnan copper administration.
translations.idiomatic: The Board of Revenue objected to machine-bureau and capital minting; the empress dowager blamed their evasion and ordered Li Hongzhang to mint at Tianjin at one mace weight. Tang Jiong was given governor rank to supervise Yunnan copper.

sentences.zh: 十四年，廣東試鑄機器錢，以重庫平七分識於幕。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year Guangdong trial-cast machine coins, marking on the reverse weight of seven fen on the treasury scale.
translations.idiomatic: In year 14 Guangdong trial-minted machine coins marked on the reverse with a weight of seven fen treasury scale.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，命直省鑄八分錢。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year provinces were ordered to cast eight-fen coins.
translations.idiomatic: In year 24 provinces were ordered to mint eight-fen coins.

sentences.zh: 而京師以制錢少，行當十錢如故。

translations.literal: But the capital, for lack of regulated cash, continued denomination-10 coins as before.
translations.idiomatic: Beijing, short of standard cash, continued the 10-cash coin as before.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，鑄銅幣當十錢，民不樂用，於是創鑄銀、銅圓，設置銀行，思劃一幣制，與東西洋各國相抗衡。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year copper coins of denomination 10 were cast; the people were unwilling to use them; therefore silver and copper dollars were newly cast, banks established, intending to unify the currency system and compete with Eastern and Western nations.
translations.idiomatic: In year 32 copper 10-cash coins were minted but rejected by the public. Silver and copper dollars and banks were then introduced to unify the currency and compete with Western powers.

sentences.zh: 初，洋商麕集粵東，西班牙、英吉利銀錢大輸入，總督林則徐謀自鑄圖抵制，以不適用而罷。

translations.literal: Initially foreign merchants gathered in eastern Guangdong; Spanish and English silver poured in; Governor Lin Zexu planned self-casting to resist it, but because it was unsuitable it was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: When foreign merchants gathered in Guangdong, Spanish and British silver flooded in. Governor Lin Zexu planned domestic coinage to counter it but abandoned the effort as impractical.

sentences.zh: 嗣是墨西哥、日本以國幣相灌輸。

translations.literal: Thereafter Mexico and Japan flooded the market with their national coins.
translations.idiomatic: Mexico and Japan then flooded the market with their national coinage.

sentences.zh: 光緒十四年，張之洞督粵，始用機器如式試鑄，李鴻章繼任續成之，文曰「光緒元寶，庫平七錢二分，廣東省造」，幕絞龍。

translations.literal: In Guangxu year 14 Zhang Zhidong governed Guangdong and first used machines to trial-cast to standard; Li Hongzhang succeeded and completed it; inscription read "Guangxu Yuanbao, seven mace two fen treasury scale, made in Guangdong Province"; reverse bore coiled dragon.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 14 Zhang Zhidong as Guangdong governor began machine trial minting; Li Hongzhang completed it. The coin read "Guangxu Yuanbao, seven mace two fen treasury scale, made in Guangdong Province" with a coiled dragon on the reverse.

sentences.zh: 並鑄三錢六分、一錢四分四釐、七分二釐、三分六釐四種小銀圓。

translations.literal: Four types of small silver dollars were also cast: three mace six fen, one mace four fen four li, seven fen two li, and three fen six li.
translations.idiomatic: Four subsidiary silver denominations were also minted: 3 mace 6 fen, 1 mace 4 fen 4 li, 7 fen 2 li, and 3 fen 6 li.

sentences.zh: 中國自行銀錢自此始。

translations.literal: China's self-minted silver coinage began from this.
translations.idiomatic: This marked the beginning of China's machine-minted silver coinage.

sentences.zh: 湖北、江西、直隸、浙江、安徽、奉天、吉林以次開鑄。

translations.literal: Hubei, Jiangxi, Zhili, Zhejiang, Anhui, Fengtian, and Jilin opened casting in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Hubei, Jiangxi, Zhili, Zhejiang, Anhui, Fengtian, and Jilin opened mints in turn.

sentences.zh: 尋以廣東、湖北、江西所鑄最稱便用，許以應解京餉撥充鑄本。

translations.literal: Soon because Guangdong, Hubei, and Jiangxi coinage was most convenient, they were permitted to use funds due to the capital as casting capital.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong, Hubei, and Jiangxi coin proved most acceptable and were allowed to use capital tribute funds as minting capital.

sentences.zh: 直省未開鑄者，飭從附鑄。

translations.literal: Provinces that had not opened mints were ordered to attach to existing mints.
translations.idiomatic: Provinces without mints were ordered to contract with existing ones.

sentences.zh: 京、外收放庫款，准搭三成。

translations.literal: Capital and provincial treasury receipts and disbursements permitted thirty percent in such coin.
translations.idiomatic: Treasury receipts and payments could include thirty percent in the new coinage.

sentences.zh: 因命劉坤一、張之洞、陶模籌議三局造鑄事宜。

translations.literal: Therefore Liu Kunyi, Zhang Zhidong, and Tao Mo were ordered to deliberate on casting at three bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kunyi, Zhang Zhidong, and Tao Mo were ordered to plan minting at three bureaus.

sentences.zh: 已復由戶部核定，七省所鑄規模成色苦參差，不利通行。

translations.literal: Later the Board of Revenue verified that the seven provinces' casting varied in size and fineness, unfavorable to circulation.
translations.idiomatic: The Board of Revenue then found that the seven provinces' coins varied in size and fineness, hindering circulation.

sentences.zh: 會造幣總廠成，擬撤其三，而留江南、直隸、廣東為分廠。

translations.literal: When the General Mint was completed, three were proposed abolished, retaining Jiangnan, Zhili, and Guangdong as branch mints.
translations.idiomatic: When the central mint was completed, three provincial mints were to close, leaving Jiangnan, Zhili, and Guangdong as branches.

sentences.zh: 初鑄准重墨圓，議者頗非之。

translations.literal: Initial casting approved heavy ink-round coins; deliberators largely criticized this.
translations.idiomatic: The initial heavy ink-round design was widely criticized.

sentences.zh: 之洞始於湖北試行一兩銀幣。

translations.literal: Zhidong first trial-issued one-tael silver coins in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhidong first trial-minted one-tael silver coins in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 戶部亦以中國立算，夙准兩錢分釐，因定主幣為庫平一兩，而以五錢、一錢小銀幣暨銅圓、制錢輔助之，令總分廠如式造行。

translations.literal: The Board of Revenue also held that China's accounting had long used taels, mace, fen, and li; therefore the main coin was fixed at one treasury-scale tael, with five-mace and one-mace small silver coins plus copper dollars and regulated cash as subsidiary; central and branch mints were ordered to cast accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: The Board fixed the main coin at one treasury-scale tael, with five-mace and one-mace subsidiary silver, copper dollars, and standard cash, and ordered central and branch mints to produce accordingly.

sentences.zh: 銅元鑄始閩、廣，江蘇繼之。

translations.literal: Copper dollars were first cast in Fujian and Guangdong; Jiangsu followed.
translations.idiomatic: Copper dollars were first minted in Fujian and Guangdong, then Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 時京局停鑄，命各運數十萬入京，由戶部發行備用。

translations.literal: At the time capital minting was suspended; each province was ordered to transport several hundred thousand to the capital for Board of Revenue issuance and reserve.
translations.idiomatic: With capital minting suspended, provinces were ordered to ship hundreds of thousands to Beijing for Board distribution.

sentences.zh: 沿江、沿海省分，並飭籌款附鑄。

translations.literal: Riverine and coastal provinces were also ordered to raise funds for attached casting.
translations.idiomatic: Coastal provinces were also ordered to fund contracted minting.

sentences.zh: 而直省陸續開鑄，造幣總廠反後成。

translations.literal: Yet provinces opened casting one after another, while the General Mint was completed later.
translations.idiomatic: Provinces opened mints one after another while the central mint was completed later.

sentences.zh: 總廠擬鑄之幣凡三品：曰金，曰銀，曰銅。

translations.literal: The general mint planned three types of coin: gold, silver, and copper.
translations.idiomatic: The central mint planned three metals: gold, silver, and copper.

sentences.zh: 最先鑄銅幣。

translations.literal: Copper coins were cast first.
translations.idiomatic: Copper was minted first.

sentences.zh: 自當制錢二十降至當二，自重四錢降而四分，凡四種，文視直省小異大同。

translations.literal: From denomination 20 regulated cash down to denomination 2, weight from four mace down to four fen, four types in all; inscriptions varied slightly among provinces but were largely the same.
translations.idiomatic: Denominations ranged from 20 to 2 cash, weight from four mace to four fen, in four types; inscriptions varied slightly by province.

sentences.zh: 直省曰「光緒元寶」，總廠初同直省，嗣定曰「大清銅幣」，皆識某所造，幕皆龍文，紫銅鑄，直省間亦用黃銅。

translations.literal: Provinces read "Guangxu Yuanbao"; the general mint at first matched provinces, later fixed as "Great Qing Copper Coin"; all marked where made; reverse all dragon design; cast in purple copper; provinces sometimes also used yellow copper.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial coins read Guangxu Yuanbao; the central mint initially matched them, then adopted Da Qing Copper Coin; all bore the mint name and a dragon reverse in purple copper, though some provinces used brass.

sentences.zh: 凡私造銅幣、偽造紙幣，罪視制錢加等。

translations.literal: Private casting of copper coins and counterfeiting paper notes were punished one degree heavier than regulated cash.
translations.idiomatic: Private copper minting and paper counterfeiting carried penalties one degree heavier than for standard cash.

sentences.zh: 初鑄銅元，為補制錢之不足，旋艷其餘利，新政餉需皆取給焉，競鑄爭售，乃至不能敷鑄本。

translations.literal: Copper dollars were first cast to supplement lack of regulated cash; soon people coveted the surplus profit; New Policy military funds all drew on it; competing casting and sales reached the point where casting capital could not be covered.
translations.idiomatic: Copper dollars were first minted to supplement scarce standard cash, but mints soon competed for profit; New Policy military funds depended on them until minting costs could not be covered.

sentences.zh: 兩江總督周馥首疏其弊，戶部為立法限制之。

translations.literal: Liangjiang Governor-General Zhou Fu first memorialized on its abuses; the Board of Revenue legislated restrictions.
translations.idiomatic: Liangjiang Governor-General Zhou Fu first memorialized on the abuses; the Board legislated restrictions.

sentences.zh: 繼與政務處上補救八事。

translations.literal: Subsequently eight remedial measures were submitted to the Bureau of Government Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Eight remedial measures were then submitted to the Bureau of Government Affairs.

sentences.zh: 旋以開鑄者多至十七省，省至二三局，恐終難言畫一，乃令山東歸併直隸，湖北歸併湖南，江南、安徽歸併江寧，浙江歸併福建，廣西歸併廣東，合奉天、河南、四川、雲貴為九廠，由部派員會辦，遣大臣周曆察核，與戶部籌定會辦事宜。

translations.literal: Soon because minting had spread to seventeen provinces with two or three bureaus each, fearing unity could never be achieved, Shandong was merged into Zhili, Hubei into Hunan, Jiangnan and Anhui into Jiangning, Zhejiang into Fujian, Guangxi into Guangdong; combining Fengtian, Henan, Sichuan, and Yunnan-Guizhou into nine mints, with ministry-appointed joint management; grand ministers were dispatched on circuit inspection; joint matters were deliberated with the Board of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: With seventeen provinces operating two or three mints each, unification seemed impossible. Shandong merged into Zhili, Hubei into Hunan, Jiangnan and Anhui into Jiangning, Zhejiang into Fujian, Guangxi into Guangdong; Fengtian, Henan, Sichuan, and Yunnan-Guizhou formed nine mints under joint ministry management, with grand ministers inspecting and coordinating with the Board.

sentences.zh: 顧銅元以積賤，當十錢僅能及半數，民私局私頗叢奸弊。

translations.literal: Yet because copper dollars accumulated in depreciation, denomination-10 coins reached only half value; private mints and private bureaus harbored many frauds.
translations.idiomatic: Copper dollars depreciated until 10-cash coins traded at half value; private mints proliferated with fraud.

sentences.zh: 應准銀者，銅元折合，類致虧損，物價翔貴，民生日益凋敝。

translations.literal: Where silver was due, conversion in copper dollars mostly caused loss; prices soared; popular livelihood daily grew impoverished.
translations.idiomatic: Payments due in silver converted to copper dollars at a loss; prices soared and livelihoods deteriorated.

sentences.zh: 省與省復相軋，至不相流通。

translations.literal: Province and province again obstructed each other, until they would not circulate mutually.
translations.idiomatic: Provinces obstructed one another until their coins would not circulate across borders.

sentences.zh: 山東巡撫袁樹勛繼陳十害。

translations.literal: Shandong Governor Yuan Shuxun subsequently memorialized ten harms.
translations.idiomatic: Shandong Governor Yuan Shuxun then memorialized ten further harms.

sentences.zh: 時總廠初鑄銅幣，尚留寶泉鑄六分制錢。

translations.literal: At the time the general mint first cast copper coins but still retained Baoquan casting six-fen regulated cash.
translations.idiomatic: When the central mint began copper coinage, Baoquan still minted six-fen standard cash.

sentences.zh: 廣東請改鑄一文錢，由總廠頒式通行。

translations.literal: Guangdong requested changing to cast one-wen coins, with the general mint issuing the standard for universal circulation.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong petitioned to mint one-wen coins under a standard issued by the central mint.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，命各銅元廠加鑄一文新錢，如銅圓式，蓋存一文舊制，藉為銅圓補救也。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year each copper-dollar mint was ordered to add casting one-wen new coins, like copper dollars in form—preserving the old one-wen system as remedy for copper dollars.
translations.idiomatic: In year 34 all copper-dollar mints were ordered to add one-wen coins in the dollar style, preserving the old denomination as a remedy for copper-dollar inflation.

sentences.zh: 自大理少卿盛宣懷奏設通商銀行，議者以東西洋各國皆有國立銀行，能持國內外財政，二十九年，允戶部請，設置官銀行，以部專其名，糾合官商資本四百萬，通用國幣、發行紙幣、官款公債皆主之。

translations.literal: From Grand Secretary of the Court of Judicial Review Sheng Xuanhuai's memorial to establish a commercial bank, deliberators held that Eastern and Western nations all had national banks able to sustain domestic and foreign finance; in the twenty-ninth year the Board of Revenue's request was approved to establish an official bank, the ministry reserving the name, combining official and merchant capital of four million, managing universal national coin, issuing paper notes, and overseeing official funds and public bonds.
translations.idiomatic: After Sheng Xuanhuai's memorial for a commercial bank, reformers noted that Western nations all had national banks sustaining domestic and foreign finance. In year 29 the Board's request was approved: an official bank with four million in official and merchant capital would manage national coinage, paper notes, official funds, and public bonds.

sentences.zh: 尋為發行紙幣，並開紙、印刷二廠。

translations.literal: Soon it issued paper notes and opened paper and printing factories.
translations.idiomatic: It soon issued paper notes and opened paper and printing factories.

sentences.zh: 會戶部改度支，更銀行名曰「大清」，設正副監督各一，造幣總廠亦如之。

translations.literal: When the Board of Revenue became the Board of Finance, the bank was renamed "Great Qing," with one chief and one deputy superintendent; the General Mint followed the same arrangement.
translations.idiomatic: When the Board of Revenue became the Board of Finance, the bank was renamed Da Qing with chief and deputy superintendents; the central mint followed suit.

sentences.zh: 銀行內並附設儲蓄銀行。

translations.literal: Within the bank a savings bank was also attached.
translations.idiomatic: A savings bank was attached within the main bank.

sentences.zh: 畫一幣制，載入各國新定商約。

translations.literal: Unification of the currency system was written into newly concluded commercial treaties with various nations.
translations.idiomatic: Currency unification was written into newly concluded commercial treaties.

sentences.zh: 部議宜先審定銀幣，試行效，則積金鑄幣三品之制，可使同條共貫。

translations.literal: Ministry deliberation held that silver coin should first be examined and fixed, trial effectiveness tested; then the system of accumulating metal to cast three types of coin could be made consistent throughout.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry held that silver coin should be standardized first; once proven, the three-metal system could be unified.

sentences.zh: 第計元計兩，尚持兩端。

translations.literal: Only whether to count by yuan or by tael still held both ends.
translations.idiomatic: Only the question of yuan versus tael accounting remained unresolved.

sentences.zh: 德宗下其事於督撫。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong referred the matter to governors-general and governors.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangxu referred the matter to provincial governors.

sentences.zh: 適有以實行商約速定幣制請者，下政務處核議，各督撫亦先後議上。

translations.literal: Just then someone petitioned to implement commercial treaties and quickly fix the currency system; it was referred to the Bureau of Government Affairs for verification; governors-general and governors also deliberated and submitted in succession.
translations.idiomatic: A petition to implement commercial treaties and fix the currency promptly went to the Bureau of Government Affairs; governors submitted opinions in turn.

sentences.zh: 主兩者至十一省，主圓者僅八省。

translations.literal: Those favoring the tael reached eleven provinces; those favoring the yuan only eight.
translations.idiomatic: Eleven provinces favored the tael; only eight favored the yuan.

sentences.zh: 度支部前亦頒布用兩，遂定一兩為主幣。

translations.literal: The Board of Finance had earlier promulgated use of the tael; therefore one tael was fixed as the main coin.
translations.idiomatic: The Board of Finance had already mandated the tael, so one tael was adopted as the main coin.

sentences.zh: 復由部設幣制調查局，而審慎於鑄造推行、畫一成色分量之間。

translations.literal: The ministry again established a Currency Investigation Bureau, deliberating carefully between casting, circulation, and unifying fineness and weight.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry also established a Currency Investigation Bureau to deliberate carefully on minting, circulation, and standardization of fineness and weight.

sentences.zh: 至宣統二年，仍前定名曰「圓」，銀幣一圓為主幣，五角、二角五、一角三種，鎳幣五分一種，銅幣二分、一分、五釐、一釐四種，為輔幣。

translations.literal: By Xuantong year 2, the earlier fixed name "yuan" was retained: one silver yuan as main coin; three subsidiary types of fifty cents, twenty-five cents, and ten cents; one nickel type of five cents; four copper types of two cents, one cent, five li, and one li.
translations.idiomatic: By Xuantong 2 the name yuan was retained: one silver yuan as the main coin, with subsidiary denominations of fifty, twenty-five, and ten cents in silver; five cents in nickel; and two, one, five-li, and one-li in copper.

sentences.zh: 銀幣重七錢二分，餘遞降。

translations.literal: Silver coins weighed seven mace two fen; the rest decreased in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The silver yuan weighed seven mace two fen; subsidiary silver coins decreased proportionally.

sentences.zh: 並撤直隸銀銅造幣廠，而留漢口、廣東、成都、雲南四廠。

translations.literal: The Zhili silver and copper mint was abolished, retaining four mints at Hankou, Guangdong, Chengdu, and Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhili mint was closed, leaving Hankou, Guangdong, Chengdu, and Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 前所鑄大小銀元，暫照市價行使，將來由總廠銀行收換改鑄。

translations.literal: Previously cast large and small silver dollars temporarily circulated at market price; in future the general mint and bank would exchange and recast them.
translations.idiomatic: Previously minted silver dollars circulated at market rates pending exchange and recasting by the central mint and bank.

sentences.zh: 三品之制，首金，次銀。

translations.literal: Among the three-metal system, gold came first, silver second.
translations.idiomatic: In the three-metal system, gold ranked first, silver second.

sentences.zh: 光緒中葉，英金磅歲騰長，每磅自華銀四兩一錢六分五釐增至八兩有奇。

translations.literal: In mid-Guangxu the British gold pound rose yearly; each pound increased from Chinese silver of four taels one mace six fen five li to over eight taels.
translations.idiomatic: In mid-Guangxu the British gold pound rose yearly from about 4.165 taels of Chinese silver to over eight taels.

sentences.zh: 御史王鵬運、通政司參議楊宜治嘗建議積金仿鑄。

translations.literal: Censor Wang Pengyun and Secretariat Councillor Yang Yizhi once proposed accumulating gold for imitation casting.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Wang Pengyun and Secretariat Councillor Yang Yizhi once proposed accumulating gold for minting.

sentences.zh: 三十年，戶部疏請備造幣之用，納官者皆準金。

translations.literal: In year 30 the Board of Revenue memorialized requesting reserves for minting; all payments to government were to be accepted in gold.
translations.idiomatic: In year 30 the Board memorialized for gold reserves for minting and accepted gold for official payments.

sentences.zh: 出使大臣汪大燮極言用金之利。

translations.literal: Envoy Wang Daxie strongly argued the benefits of using gold.
translations.idiomatic: Envoy Wang Daxie strongly advocated adopting gold.

sentences.zh: 孫寶琦則請對內用銀，對外必預計用金。

translations.literal: Sun Baoqi then requested using silver domestically but necessarily planning gold for foreign use.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Baoqi urged silver domestically but gold reserves for foreign transactions.

sentences.zh: 廷臣之論國幣者，亦以不臻至用金，幣制不為完善，皆請速定用本位金，卒未能實行雲。

translations.literal: Court ministers discussing national coin also held that without reaching use of gold, the currency system was not complete; all requested quickly fixing gold as the standard; in the end it could not be implemented.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers debating national currency held that without a gold standard the system was incomplete and urged rapid adoption—but gold never was implemented.

sentences.zh: 茶法我國產茶之地，惟江蘇、安徽、江西、浙江、福建、四川、兩湖、雲、貴為最。

translations.literal: Tea law: In our country the tea-producing regions were chiefly Jiangsu, Anhui, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Sichuan, the two Huguang provinces, Yunnan, and Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On tea administration: China's chief tea-producing provinces were Jiangsu, Anhui, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Sichuan, Huguang, Yunnan, and Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 明時茶法有三：曰官茶，儲邊易馬；

translations.literal: In Ming times there were three tea systems: official tea, stored on the frontier to exchange for horses;
translations.idiomatic: Under the Ming there were three tea systems: official tea, stored on the frontier to trade for horses;

sentences.zh: 曰商茶，給引徵課；

translations.literal: merchant tea, issued licenses and levied duties;
translations.idiomatic: merchant tea, licensed and taxed;

sentences.zh: 曰貢茶，則上用也。

translations.literal: tribute tea, for imperial use.
translations.idiomatic: and tribute tea for imperial use.

sentences.zh: 清因之。

translations.literal: The Qing followed this.
