translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, it was approved that Gansu, following the Huai salt precedent, use tickets in place of transport permits; regardless of province, all merchants were ordered first to pay regular duty before tickets could be issued.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 13, Gansu was approved to follow the Huai salt model, replacing transport permits with tickets; merchants from any province had to pay regular duty before receiving a ticket.

sentences.zh: 其雜課歸併釐稅項下徵收。

translations.literal: Miscellaneous duties were merged and collected under the surtax item.
translations.idiomatic: Miscellaneous fees were folded into the surtax.

sentences.zh: 各項名色概予刪除。

translations.literal: All separate categories were broadly deleted.
translations.idiomatic: Separate fee categories were abolished.

sentences.zh: 行銷內地者，照納正課三兩外，於行銷地各完釐稅，每引以一兩數錢為度，多不過二兩。

translations.literal: For sale within the interior, besides paying regular duty of three taels, surtax was paid at each place of sale, with one-odd taels per permit as the measure and no more than two taels.
translations.idiomatic: For domestic sale, besides three taels of regular duty, surtax was paid where tea was sold—generally one-odd taels per permit, never more than two.

sentences.zh: 出口之茶，則另於邊境局卡加完釐一次，以示區別。

translations.literal: Tea for export paid surtax once more at frontier stations and passes, to show the distinction.
translations.idiomatic: Export tea paid one additional surtax at frontier checkpoints to mark the distinction.

sentences.zh: 光緒十年，戶部統籌財政，於茶法略言：「據總理衙門單開，光緒八、九等年出口茶數多至萬九千餘萬斤。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Guangxu, the Board of Revenue, coordinating finances, stated briefly on tea law: "According to a list from the Zongli Yamen, in the eighth, ninth, and other years of Guangxu export tea reached more than 190 million catties.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 10, coordinating finances, the Board of Revenue summarized tea law: "The Zongli Yamen reported that in Guangxu 8–9 export tea exceeded 1.9 billion catties.

sentences.zh: 查道光年間英國所收茶稅，約每百斤收銀五十兩，而我之出口稅僅納二兩五錢，不及十一。

translations.literal: Investigation shows that in the Daoguang period Britain's tea tax collected about fifty taels of silver per hundred catties, while our export tax paid only two taels five mace—not one-eleventh of theirs.
translations.idiomatic: In the Daoguang era Britain collected about fifty taels of tea tax per hundred catties, while China's export duty was only two taels five mace—less than one-eleventh as much.

sentences.zh: 擬照甘肅茶封之例，每五十斤就園戶徵銀三錢。

translations.literal: It was proposed to follow the Gansu tea-package precedent and collect three mace of silver from growers per fifty catties.
translations.idiomatic: It was proposed to follow the Gansu tea-package model and levy three mace per fifty catties directly on growers.

sentences.zh: 增課既多，洋人無所藉口。

translations.literal: Since the increased duty was substantial, foreigners would have no pretext.
translations.idiomatic: With a substantial increase, foreigners would have no grounds for complaint.

sentences.zh: 或照寧夏、延、榆、綏等處茶引每道徵銀三兩九錢之例，於產茶處所設局驗茶，發給部頒茶照，每照百斤，徵銀三兩九錢，經過內地關卡，另納釐稅，驗照蓋戳放行，不準重複影射。

translations.literal: Or, following the precedent at Ningxia, Yan'an, Yulin, Suide, and other places of three taels nine mace per tea transport permit, offices would be established at tea-producing places to inspect tea and issue Board-distributed tea licenses; each license for one hundred catties would collect three taels nine mace; passing inland passes and stations, surtax would be paid separately; licenses would be inspected, stamped, and release granted, with duplicate evasion forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Alternatively, following Ningxia, Yan'an, Yulin, and Suide, where each permit drew three taels nine mace, inspection offices at production sites would issue Board licenses at three taels nine mace per hundred catties; inland checkpoints would collect surtax separately, stamp the license, and forbid duplicate evasion.

sentences.zh: 所有茶照，按年豫行赴督請領，原照一年後作廢。

translations.literal: All tea licenses were to be requested annually in advance from the governor; original licenses were void after one year.
translations.idiomatic: Licenses would be requested annually from the governor in advance and expire after one year.

sentences.zh: 或於產茶處所驗茶發給部照，既完課三兩，再倍收銀三兩九錢，前後共徵七兩八錢，一切雜費均予豁除。

translations.literal: Or at tea-producing places tea would be inspected and Board licenses issued; after regular duty of three taels was paid, three taels nine mace would be collected again at double rate, seven taels eight mace in all before and after, and all miscellaneous fees would be waived.
translations.idiomatic: Alternatively, at production sites tea would be inspected and Board licenses issued: three taels of regular duty plus another three taels nine mace, seven taels eight mace in total, with all miscellaneous fees abolished.

sentences.zh: 惟於各海關及邊卡，凡應納洋稅，仍照向章完納。

translations.literal: Only at each maritime customs and frontier station, wherever foreign duty was due, payment would still follow former regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Foreign duties at maritime customs and frontier stations would still be paid under existing rules.

sentences.zh: 若在內地行銷販運，無論經過何省何處釐卡關榷，均免再徵。

translations.literal: If sold and transported within the interior, no matter through which province or surtax station or pass duty was passed, no further levy would be collected.
translations.idiomatic: For domestic sale and transport, no further levy would be collected at any provincial surtax station or pass.

sentences.zh: 則改釐為課，改散為總，既便稽查，復免侵漁。

translations.literal: Thus surtax would become regular duty, scattered collection would become consolidated collection; inspection would be convenient and extortion avoided.
translations.idiomatic: Converting surtax into regular duty and scattered levies into a single payment would ease inspection and curb extortion.

sentences.zh: 惟園戶及販商若何防其走漏，應令各省參酌定章，覆奏辦理。

translations.literal: Only how to prevent leakage by growers and traveling merchants should be left to each province to deliberate and fix regulations, and report back for handling.
translations.idiomatic: Each province should decide how to prevent evasion by growers and traders and report back with regulations.

sentences.zh: 十二年，以山西商人在理籓院領票，詭稱運銷蒙古地方，實私販湖茶，侵銷新疆南北兩路。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, because Shanxi merchants obtained tickets at the Lifan Yuan and falsely claimed to transport and sell to Mongol territories while in fact privately trafficking Hunan tea and encroaching on sales in both northern and southern routes of Xinjiang,
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 12, Shanxi merchants were obtaining Lifan Yuan tickets claiming Mongol destinations while smuggling Hunan tea into both northern and southern Xinjiang.

sentences.zh: 一票數年，循環轉運，往往逃釐漏稅。

translations.literal: one ticket served for several years in repeated circulation, often evading surtax and leaking tax.
translations.idiomatic: A single ticket might circulate for years, repeatedly evading surtax and duty.

sentences.zh: 經部奏准，嗣後領票，註明「不準販運私茶」字樣。

translations.literal: the Board memorialized and it was approved that thereafter on issued tickets the words "private tea transport and sale not permitted" would be noted.
translations.idiomatic: The Board approved that future tickets must bear the notation "private tea not permitted."

sentences.zh: 如欲辦官茶，即赴甘肅領票繳課完釐。

translations.literal: If one wished to handle official tea, one should go to Gansu to obtain tickets and pay duty and surtax.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants handling official tea had to obtain Gansu tickets and pay duty and surtax there.

sentences.zh: 倘復運銷私茶，查出沒官。

translations.literal: If private tea was again transported and sold, on discovery it would be confiscated by the state.
translations.idiomatic: Private tea found in transit would be confiscated.

sentences.zh: 是時泰西諸國嗜茶者眾，日本、印度、意大利艷其利厚，雖天時地質遜於我國，然精心講求種植之法，所產遂多。

translations.literal: At this time many in Western countries were fond of tea; Japan, India, and Italy envied its thick profits. Although climate and soil were inferior to our country, they carefully studied planting methods, and production therefore grew abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Western nations had grown tea-mad; Japan, India, and Italy, drawn by the profits, studied cultivation carefully despite inferior climate and soil, and their output rose sharply.

sentences.zh: 蓋印度種茶，在道光十四年，至光緒三年乃大盛。

translations.literal: India planted tea in the fourteenth year of Daoguang; only in the third year of Guangxu did it flourish greatly.
translations.idiomatic: India began planting tea in Daoguang 14; it did not flourish until Guangxu 3.

sentences.zh: 錫蘭、意大利其繼起者也。

translations.literal: Ceylon and Italy were those that rose afterward.
translations.idiomatic: Ceylon and Italy followed.

sentences.zh: 法蘭西既得越南，亦令種茶，有東山、建吉、富華諸園。

translations.literal: France, having taken Vietnam, also ordered tea planted; there were estates at Dongshan, Jianji, and Fuhua.
translations.idiomatic: After France took Vietnam, it ordered tea planted at estates such as Dongshan, Jianji, and Fuhua.

sentences.zh: 美利堅於咸豐八年購吾國茶秧萬株，發給農民，其後愈購愈多，歲發茶秧至十二萬株，足供其國之用。

translations.literal: The United States in the eighth year of Xianfeng purchased ten thousand tea seedlings from our country and distributed them to farmers; afterward purchases grew ever larger, until twelve thousand seedlings were sent annually, enough to supply the country's needs.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 8 the United States bought ten thousand tea seedlings from China for its farmers; purchases soon rose to twelve thousand seedlings a year, enough for domestic supply.

sentences.zh: 故我國光緒十年以前輸出之數甚鉅，未幾漸為所奪。

translations.literal: Therefore before the tenth year of Guangxu our country's export volume was very great; before long it was gradually seized from us.
translations.idiomatic: China's exports were enormous before Guangxu 10, but were soon overtaken.

sentences.zh: 印度茶往英國者，歲約七十三萬二千石，價約二千四萬兩。

translations.literal: Indian tea sent to Britain amounted yearly to about 732,000 piculs, worth about 2.4 million taels.
translations.idiomatic: India sent about 732,000 piculs of tea to Britain each year, worth roughly 2.4 million taels.

sentences.zh: 吾國茶往者八十九萬八千石，價約千八百六十八萬兩。

translations.literal: Our country's tea sent there amounted to 898,000 piculs, worth about 18.68 million taels.
translations.idiomatic: China sent 898,000 piculs, worth about 18.68 million taels.

sentences.zh: 印度茶少於華，而價反多。

translations.literal: Indian tea was less than China's, yet the price was greater in reverse.
translations.idiomatic: India sent less tea than China, yet fetched higher prices.

sentences.zh: 迨二十二年我國運往，乃止二十一萬九千四百餘石而已。

translations.literal: By the twenty-second year what our country transported there was only a little more than 219,400 piculs.
translations.idiomatic: By Guangxu 22 China's shipments had fallen to just over 219,400 piculs.

sentences.zh: 日本之茶，多售於美國，亦有運至我國者。

translations.literal: Japan's tea was mostly sold to the United States; some was also transported to our country.
translations.idiomatic: Most Japanese tea went to the United States, though some reached China.

sentences.zh: 光緒十三年，我茶往日本者萬二千餘石，而彼茶進口萬六千餘石。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Guangxu, our tea sent to Japan was a little more than 12,000 piculs, while their tea imported was a little more than 16,000 piculs.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 13 China exported a little over 12,000 piculs of tea to Japan while importing over 16,000 piculs of Japanese tea.

sentences.zh: 其專尚華茶取用宏多者惟俄。

translations.literal: Of those who exclusively favored Chinese tea and used it in great quantity, only Russia.
translations.idiomatic: Only Russia still relied heavily on Chinese tea.

sentences.zh: 蓋自哈薩克、浩罕諸部新屬於彼，地加廣，人加眾，需物加多，而茶尤為所賴。

translations.literal: Since the Kazakh and Kokand regions newly belonged to them, territory grew wider, people more numerous, needs greater, and tea above all was what they relied on.
translations.idiomatic: With Kazakhstan and Kokand newly under Russian rule, its territory and population grew, demand rose, and tea above all remained essential.

sentences.zh: 光緒七年定約，允以嘉峪關為通商口岸，而往來益盛。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Guangxu a treaty was fixed, allowing Jiayu Pass as a treaty port, and traffic grew ever more flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: The Guangxu 7 treaty made Jiayu Pass a trading port, and traffic flourished.

sentences.zh: 十年後我國運往之茶，居全數三之一。

translations.literal: Ten years later tea transported from our country accounted for one-third of the whole.
translations.idiomatic: Ten years on, Chinese tea still accounted for one-third of Russia's supply.

sentences.zh: 十三年，並雜貨計，出口價九百二萬兩有奇，而進口價僅十一萬八千餘兩，凡輸自我者八百九十萬兩。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, counting miscellaneous goods together, export value was a little more than 9.2 million taels, while import value was only a little more than 118,000 taels; what was supplied from us totaled 8.9 million taels.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 13, including miscellaneous goods, exports were worth over 9.2 million taels against imports of just over 118,000 taels—a net outflow from China of 8.9 million taels.

sentences.zh: 然十二年茶少價多，十三年茶多價少，華商已有受困之勢，厥後亦兼購於他國，用此華茶之利驟減。

translations.literal: Yet in the twelfth year tea was scarce and prices high; in the thirteenth year tea was abundant and prices low; Chinese merchants already showed signs of distress, and afterward they also bought from other countries, so the profit of Chinese tea sharply diminished.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 12 tea was scarce and prices high; in Guangxu 13 supply rose and prices fell. Chinese merchants were already under pressure, and as Russia also bought elsewhere, China's tea profits collapsed.

sentences.zh: 蓋我國自昔視茶為農家餘事，惟以隙地營之，又採摘不時，焙制無術，其為他人所傾，勢所必至。

translations.literal: Our country from old regarded tea as a farm family's spare occupation, cultivating it only on leftover land, picking at improper times, and lacking skill in roasting; that others should overturn it was inevitable by tendency.
translations.idiomatic: China had long treated tea as a sideline crop, grown on spare plots, picked at the wrong season, and poorly processed; being overtaken was inevitable.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，茶葉公會以狀陳於度支部，稅務司亦以茶稅減少為言，於是命籌整理之策。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year, the Tea Guild presented a petition to the Ministry of Finance; the Tax Bureau also spoke of reduced tea tax, and orders were then issued to plan remedial measures.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 33 the Tea Guild petitioned the Ministry of Finance, and the Tax Bureau reported falling tea revenues; the court ordered remedial measures drawn up.

sentences.zh: 宣統初，農工商部遂有酌免稅釐之議。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xuantong, the Ministry of Agriculture, Industry, and Commerce then had a proposal to consider exemption from tax and surtax.
translations.idiomatic: In early Xuantong the Ministry of Agriculture, Industry, and Commerce proposed tax and surtax relief.

sentences.zh: 漢口、福州皆自外國購入制茶機器，且由印度聘熟練教師。

translations.literal: Hankou and Fuzhou both purchased tea-processing machinery from foreign countries and also hired skilled teachers from India.
translations.idiomatic: Hankou and Fuzhou imported tea-processing machinery and hired skilled instructors from India.

sentences.zh: 江西巡撫又籌款貸與茶戶。

translations.literal: The Jiangxi governor also raised funds and lent them to tea growers.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangxi governor also raised funds to lend to tea growers.

sentences.zh: 自是銷入歐洲及北阿非利加洲者乃稍暢旺。

translations.literal: From this time sales into Europe and North Africa became somewhat smoother and more flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: Sales to Europe and North Africa then improved somewhat.

sentences.zh: 夫吾國茶質本勝諸國，往往澀味中含有香氣，能使舌本回甘，泰西人名曰「膽念」，他國所產鮮能及此。

translations.literal: Our country's tea quality in origin surpassed all countries; often within astringency there was fragrance that could make the root of the tongue return sweet; Westerners named it "danian," and tea produced by other countries rarely matched this.
translations.idiomatic: Chinese tea was inherently superior: its astringency often carried a fragrance that left a sweet aftertaste on the palate—what Westerners call "tanin"—a quality rarely matched elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 故日本雖有茶，必購於我，荷蘭使臣克羅伯亦言爪哇、印度、錫蘭茶皆不如華茶遠甚。

translations.literal: Therefore although Japan had tea, it had to purchase from us; Dutch envoy Kolff also said that tea from Java, India, and Ceylon was far inferior to Chinese tea.
translations.idiomatic: Japan still had to buy Chinese tea despite its own production, and Dutch envoy Kolff declared Java, Indian, and Ceylon teas far inferior to China's.

sentences.zh: 然則獎勵保護，無使天然物產為彼族人力所奪，是不能不有望於今之言商務者。

translations.literal: If so, encouragement and protection so that natural products would not be seized by others' labor—this could not but be hoped for from those who speak of commerce today.
translations.idiomatic: Encouragement and protection are needed so that nature's bounty is not lost to foreign industry—and much must be expected of those who speak for commerce today.

sentences.zh: 礦政清初鑒於明代競言礦利，中使四齣，暴斂病民，於是聽民採取，輸稅於官，皆有常率。

translations.literal: Mining administration: in the early Qing, seeing that the Ming had competed to speak of mining profit, eunuch envoys went out on four sides, and violent exaction harmed the people; therefore the people were allowed to extract, paying tax to the state, all with fixed rates.
translations.idiomatic: Mining administration: Early in the Qing, mindful that the Ming had chased mining profits through eunuch agents who extorted the people, the court allowed private extraction with tax paid to the state at fixed rates.

sentences.zh: 若有礙禁山風水，民田廬墓，及聚眾擾民，或歲歉穀踴，輒用封禁。

translations.literal: If there was harm to protected mountains and geomantic sites, civilian fields, houses, and tombs, or gathering crowds to disturb the people, or years of poor harvest with grain prices soaring, closure and prohibition were promptly applied.
translations.idiomatic: Mines were closed when they threatened protected mountains, geomantic sites, farmland, homes, or tombs; when crowds caused disorder; or when famine drove grain prices up.

sentences.zh: 世祖初開山東臨朐、招遠銀礦，順治八年罷之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Shizu reign, silver mines at Linqu and Zhaoyuan in Shandong were opened; in the eighth year of Shunzhi they were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shunzhi's reign silver mines at Linqu and Zhaoyuan in Shandong were opened; they were shut in Shunzhi 8.

sentences.zh: 十四年，開古北、喜峰等口鐵礦。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, iron mines at Gubei, Xifeng, and other passes were opened.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 14 iron mines at Gubei, Xifeng, and other passes were opened.

sentences.zh: 康熙間，遣官監采山西應州、陝西臨潼、山東萊陽銀礦。

translations.literal: During the Kangxi period, officials were dispatched to supervise extraction of silver mines at Yingzhou in Shanxi, Lintong in Shaanxi, and Laiyang in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Under Kangxi, officials supervised silver mining at Yingzhou in Shanxi, Lintong in Shaanxi, and Laiyang in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，悉行停止。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, all were stopped.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 22 all were shut down.

sentences.zh: 並諭開礦無益地方，嗣後有請開採者，均不準行。

translations.literal: It was also decreed that opening mines benefited not the locality; hereafter whoever petitioned to open and extract would uniformly not be permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The court also ruled that mining did local communities no good and denied all future petitions to open mines.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，群臣多言礦利。

translations.literal: When Shizong took the throne, many among the officials spoke of mining profit.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yongzheng Emperor ascended the throne, many officials urged the profit to be had from mining.

sentences.zh: 粵督孔毓珣、粵撫楊文乾、湘撫布蘭泰、廣西提督田畯、廣東布政使王士俊、四川提督黃廷桂相繼疏請開礦，均不準行，或嚴旨切責。

translations.literal: Guangdong governor-general Kong Yuxun, Guangdong governor Yang Wenqian, Hunan governor Bulate, Guangxi provincial military commander Tian Jun, Guangdong provincial treasurer Wang Shijun, and Sichuan provincial military commander Huang Tinggui successively memorialized requesting to open mines; all were not permitted, or were sharply rebuked by stern edict.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong governor-general Kong Yuxun, Guangdong governor Yang Wenqian, Hunan governor Bulate, Guangxi military commander Tian Jun, Guangdong treasurer Wang Shijun, and Sichuan military commander Huang Tinggui petitioned in turn to open mines; all were refused, some with stern imperial rebukes.

sentences.zh: 十三年，粵督鄂彌達請開惠、潮、韶、肇等府礦，下九卿議行。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, Guangdong governor-general E Midar requested opening mines in the prefectures of Huizhou, Chaozhou, Shaozhou, Zhaoqing, and others; the matter was referred to the Nine Ministers for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 13, Guangdong governor-general E Midar petitioned to open mines in Huizhou, Chaozhou, Shaozhou, Zhaoqing, and other prefectures; the memorial was sent to the Nine Ministers, who recommended approval.

sentences.zh: 上以妨本務停止。

translations.literal: The emperor, on grounds that it would hinder fundamental duties, stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor halted the plan, holding that mining would distract from essential governance.

sentences.zh: 蓋粵東山多田少，而礦產最繁，土民習於攻采。

translations.literal: For eastern Guangdong had many mountains and little farmland, while mineral resources were most abundant, and local people were practiced in mining and extraction.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong had more mountains than arable land and the richest mineral deposits; locals were skilled miners.

sentences.zh: 礦峒所在，千百為群，往往聚眾私掘，嘯聚剽掠。

translations.literal: Where mine tunnels were located, hundreds and thousands formed groups; they often gathered crowds to dig privately, banded together, and raided.
translations.idiomatic: At mining sites hundreds or thousands gathered, often mining illegally in bands that looted and pillaged.

sentences.zh: 故其時礦東開礦，較他省尤為厲禁。

translations.literal: Therefore at that time opening mines in eastern Guangdong was prohibited more severely than in other provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Opening mines in Guangdong was therefore banned more strictly than anywhere else.

sentences.zh: 滇銅自官為經理，嗣由官給工本。

translations.literal: Yunnan copper was from the start managed by the state; afterward working capital was provided by the state.
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan copper was initially state-managed; later the government supplied operating capital.

sentences.zh: 雍正初，歲出銅八九十萬，不數年，且二三百萬，歲供本路鼓鑄。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongzheng, yearly output was eight or nine hundred thousand [jin]; within a few years it reached two or three million, yearly supplying local coin casting.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongzheng annual output was eight or nine hundred thousand jin; within a few years it rose to two or three million, supplying local mints.

sentences.zh: 及運湖廣、江西，僅百萬有奇。

translations.literal: When transported to Huguang and Jiangxi, only slightly over one million.
translations.idiomatic: Shipments to Huguang and Jiangxi totaled just over one million jin.

sentences.zh: 乾隆初，歲發銅本銀百萬兩，四五年間，歲出六七百萬或八九百萬，最多乃至千二三百萬。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianlong, one million taels of copper capital were issued yearly; within four or five years yearly output was six or seven million or eight or nine million, at most reaching twelve or thirteen million.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qianlong the state advanced one million taels of capital yearly; within four or five years output reached six to nine million jin annually, peaking at twelve or thirteen million.

sentences.zh: 戶、工兩局，暨江南、江西、浙江、福建、陝西、湖北、廣東、廣西、貴州九路，歲需九百餘萬，悉取給焉。

translations.literal: The two Boards of Revenue and Works, together with the nine routes of Jiangnan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Shaanxi, Hubei, Guangdong, Guangxi, and Guizhou, yearly required over nine million, all supplied from there.
translations.idiomatic: The Revenue and Works boards and nine provincial mint routes—Jiangnan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, Fujian, Shaanxi, Hubei, Guangdong, Guangxi, and Guizhou—needed over nine million jin yearly, all drawn from Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 礦廠以湯丹、碌碌、大水、茂麓、獅子山、大功為最，寧台、金釵、義都、發古山、九度、萬象次之。

translations.literal: Among mining works Tangdan, Lulu, Dashui, Maolu, Shizishan, and Dagong ranked highest; Ningtai, Jinchai, Yidu, Fagushan, Jiudu, and Wanxiang ranked next.
translations.idiomatic: The leading mines were Tangdan, Lulu, Dashui, Maolu, Lion Mountain, and Dagong; Ningtai, Jinchai, Yidu, Fagushan, Jiudu, and Wanxiang came next.

sentences.zh: 大廠礦丁六七萬，次亦萬餘。

translations.literal: Major works had sixty or seventy thousand miners; secondary ones also over ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Major works employed sixty or seventy thousand miners; smaller ones still had more than ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 近則土民遠及黔、粵，仰食礦利者，奔走相屬。

translations.literal: Nearby local people and, distantly, those from Guizhou and Guangdong who depended on mining profit for livelihood came in unbroken succession.
translations.idiomatic: Locals and, from as far as Guizhou and Guangdong, those who lived off mining profits flocked there in steady streams.

sentences.zh: 正廠峒老砂竭，輒開子廠以補其額。

translations.literal: When the old ore of main-work tunnels was exhausted, subsidiary works were promptly opened to make up the quota.
translations.idiomatic: When main pits ran out, subsidiary mines were opened at once to meet quotas.

sentences.zh: 故滇省銅政，累葉程功，非他項礦產可比。

translations.literal: Therefore Yunnan's copper administration, measured in achievement over successive reigns, was not comparable to other mineral products.
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan's copper administration, built up over generations, stood alone among mining enterprises.

sentences.zh: 是年海防議起，直隸總督李鴻章、船政大臣沈葆楨請開採煤鐵以濟軍需，上允其請，命於直隸磁州、福建台灣試辦。

translations.literal: That year the coastal-defense debate arose; Zhili governor-general Li Hongzhang and Minister of the Naval Yards Shen Baozhen requested opening coal and iron extraction to meet military needs; the emperor approved their request and ordered trial operations at Cizhou in Zhili and Taiwan in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: That year the coastal-defense debate began; Zhili governor-general Li Hongzhang and naval minister Shen Baozhen petitioned to open coal and iron mines for military supply; the emperor agreed and ordered trial operations at Cizhou in Zhili and in Taiwan, Fujian.

sentences.zh: 光緒八年，兩江總督左宗棠亦言北洋籌辦防務，製造船砲，及各省機器輪船所需煤鐵，最為大宗，請開辦江蘇利國驛煤鐵。

translations.literal: In Guangxu 8, Liangjiang governor-general Zuo Zongtang also stated that in preparing northern coastal defenses, building ships and cannon, and supplying coal and iron needed by steamships and machinery in each province, these were the greatest bulk requirements; he requested opening the Liguo Postal Station coal and iron mine in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 8, Liangjiang governor-general Zuo Zongtang argued that northern coastal defense, shipbuilding, artillery, and the coal and iron consumed by provincial steam machinery made mining the top priority, and petitioned to open the Liguo postal station coal and iron works in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 報聞。

translations.literal: The report was received.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was noted.

sentences.zh: 嗣是以次修築鐵路，煤鐵益為當務之急。

translations.literal: Thereafter railways were built in succession, and coal and iron became all the more the urgent task of the day.
translations.idiomatic: As railways were built one after another, coal and iron became more urgent than ever.

sentences.zh: 於是煤礦則吉林大石頭頂子、亂泥溝、半拉窩、雞溝、二道河、陶家屯、石牌嶺，黑龍江太平山、察漢敖拉卡倫，直隸開平、唐山，內丘縣之上坪、永固、磁窯溝、南陽寨，臨城縣之岡頭、石固、膠泥溝、楊家溝、新莊、竹壁、牟村、焦村，宣化府之雞鳴、玉帶、八寶寺山，阜平縣炭灰鋪村，曲陽縣白石溝、野北村，張家口廳海拉坎山、馬連圪達，宛平縣青龍澗、碑碣子，承德府榆樹溝，奉天海龍府遠來、義和、進寶、玉盛、永順、永益、萬利、人和、同德、順發，錦州府大窯溝，錦西廳碭石溝，本溪縣王乾溝，興京廳蜜蜂溝，遼陽州窯子峪，江西萍鄉、永新、餘干，山東嶧縣，安徽貴池、廣德、繁昌、東流、涇縣，湖北荊門，河南禹州，山西平定、鳳台，浙江桐廬、餘杭，江蘇上元、句容，湖南湘鄉、祁陽，廣西富川、賀縣、奉議、恩陽、南寧、那坡，陝西白水、澄城、同官、宜君、邠州、隴州、淳化。

translations.literal: Thereupon, for coal mines: in Jilin—Dashidingzi, Luannigou, Banlawo, Jigou, Erdaohe, Taojiatun, and Shipailing; in Heilongjiang—Taiping Mountain and Chahan Aolakalun; in Zhili—Kaiping and Tangshan; in Neiqiu County—Shangping, Yonggu, Ciyaogou, and Nanyangzhai; in Linqiu County—Gangtou, Shigu, Jiaonigou, Yangjiagou, Xinzhuang, Zhubi, Moucun, and Jiaocun; in Xuanhua Prefecture—Jiming, Yudai, and Babaosi Mountain; in Fuping County—Tanhuipu Village; in Quyang County—Baishigou and Yebei Village; in Zhangjiakou Department—Hailakanshan and Maliangeda; in Wanping County—Qinglongjian and Beijiezi; in Chengde Prefecture—Yushugou; in Fengtian at Hailong Prefecture—Yuanlai, Yihe, Jinbao, Yusheng, Yongshun, Yongyi, Wanli, Renhe, Tongde, and Shunfa; in Jinzhou Prefecture—Dayao Gou; in Jinxi Department—Dangshigou; in Benxi County—Wangqiangou; in Xingjing Department—Mifenggou; in Liaoyang Prefecture—Yaoziyu; in Jiangxi—Pingxiang, Yongxin, and Yugan; in Shandong—Yi County; in Anhui—Guichi, Guangde, Fanchang, Dongliu, and Jing County; in Hubei—Jingmen; in Henan—Yuzhou; in Shanxi—Pingding and Fengtai; in Zhejiang—Tonglu and Yuhang; in Jiangsu—Shangyuan and Jurong; in Hunan—Xiangxiang and Qiyang; in Guangxi—Fuchuan, Hexian, Fengyi, Enyang, Nanning, and Napo; in Shaanxi—Baishui, Chengcheng, Tongguan, Yijun, Binzhou, Longzhou, and Chunhua.
translations.idiomatic: Coal mines opened across the empire: in Jilin at Dashidingzi, Luannigou, Banlawo, Jigou, Erdaohe, Taojiatun, and Shipailing; in Heilongjiang at Taiping Mountain and Chahan Aolakalun; in Zhili at Kaiping and Tangshan; and at scores of sites in Neiqiu, Linqiu, Xuanhua, Fuping, Quyang, Zhangjiakou, Wanping, Chengde, Fengtian, Jinzhou, Jinxi, Benxi, Xingjing, Liaoyang, Jiangxi, Shandong, Anhui, Hubei, Henan, Shanxi, Zhejiang, Jiangsu, Hunan, Guangxi, and Shaanxi—as named in the text.

sentences.zh: 鐵礦則直隸遷安縣、灤州，湖北大冶，廣西永寧州，江西永新縣，雲南開、廣兩府，貴州青谿，皆先後開採，而秦、晉商民零星開採，尤難悉數。

translations.literal: For iron mines: Qian'an County and Luanzhou in Zhili, Daye in Hubei, Yongning Prefecture in Guangxi, Yongxin County in Jiangxi, Kai and Guang prefectures in Yunnan, and Qingxi in Guizhou—all were opened and extracted in succession; while merchants and people of Shaanxi and Shanxi opened and extracted sporadically, especially difficult to enumerate fully.
translations.idiomatic: Iron mines opened in turn at Qian'an County and Luanzhou in Zhili, Daye in Hubei, Yongning in Guangxi, Yongxin in Jiangxi, Kai and Guang prefectures in Yunnan, and Qingxi in Guizhou; small-scale mining by merchants from Shaanxi and Shanxi was too scattered to count.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，詔開辦各省金銀礦廠。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, an edict ordered opening gold and silver mining works in each province.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 22 an edict called for gold and silver mines to be opened in every province.

sentences.zh: 自光緒初年，開直隸窯溝銀礦，甘肅西寧、甘、涼，黑龍江漠河觀音山、奇乾河各金礦外無聞焉。

translations.literal: From the early Guangxu period, apart from the Yaogou silver mine in Zhili and the gold mines at Guanyin Mountain and Qi Gan River in Mohe, Heilongjiang, and those at Xining, Gan, and Liang in Gansu, nothing was heard of elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Before the edict, only a few were known from early Guangxu: the Yaogou silver mine in Zhili; gold mines at Xining, Gan, and Liang in Gansu; and at Guanyin Mountain and Qi Gan River in Mohe, Heilongjiang.

sentences.zh: 自明令頒行而後，金礦則直隸之平泉州屬轉山子，建昌縣屬金廠溝，撫寧縣屬雙山子，濼平縣屬寬溝，豐寧縣大營子、西碾子溝，翁牛特旗之紅花溝、水泉溝、拐棒溝，而遷安縣所產尤旺。

translations.literal: After the clear edict was promulgated, gold mines included Zhuanshanzi under Pingquan Prefecture, Zhili; Jinchanggou under Jianchang County; Shuangshanzi under Funing County; Kuangou under Luanping County; Dayingzi and Xinianzigou in Fengning County; Honghuagou, Shuiquangou, and Guaibanggou in Ongniud Banner; and output from Qian'an County was especially rich.
translations.idiomatic: After the edict took effect, gold mines opened across Zhili—including Zhuanshanzi in Pingquan, Jinchanggou in Jianchang, Shuangshanzi in Funing, Kuangou in Luanping, Dayingzi and Xinianzigou in Fengning, and Honghuagou, Shuiquangou, and Guaibanggou in Ongniud Banner—with Qian'an County proving especially productive.

sentences.zh: 奉天之鳳凰、安東、遼陽、通化、寬甸、懷仁、鐵嶺、開原、通化、海城、錦縣，蒙古之賀連溝、大小槽、碾溝、除虎溝、硃家溝、板橋子、珠爾琥珠、克勒司、布恭、特勒基、哈拉格囊圖、奎騰河、圖什業圖汗，四川之冕溝，湖南之平江，浙江之諸暨，黑龍江之黑河，新疆之和闐、焉耆。

translations.literal: In Fengtian—Fenghuang, Andong, Liaoyang, Tonghua, Kuandian, Huairen, Tieling, Kaiyuan, Tonghua, Haicheng, and Jin County; in Mongolia—Heliangou, Daxiao Cao, Niangou, Chuhugou, Zhujiagou, Banqiaozi, Zhu'erhuzhu, Kelesi, Bugong, Teleji, Halagenangtu, Kuiteng River, and Tushiyetu Khan; in Sichuan—Miangou; in Hunan—Pingjiang; in Zhejiang—Zhuji; in Heilongjiang—Heihe; in Xinjiang—Hotan and Yanqi.
translations.idiomatic: Further gold mines opened in Fengtian (Fenghuang, Andong, Liaoyang, Tonghua, Kuandian, Huairen, Tieling, Kaiyuan, Haicheng, and Jin County), Mongolia (numerous sites including Heliangou, Daxiao Cao, and Tushiyetu Khan), Sichuan (Miangou), Hunan (Pingjiang), Zhejiang (Zhuji), Heilongjiang (Heihe), and Xinjiang (Hotan and Yanqi).

sentences.zh: 銀礦則四川之天全、盧山、大穴山頭，皆報明開採。

translations.literal: For silver mines, Tianquan, Lushan, and Daxue Shantou in Sichuan all reported and declared opening and extraction.
translations.idiomatic: Silver mines at Tianquan, Lushan, and Daxue Shantou in Sichuan were all registered and opened.

sentences.zh: 而銅、錫、鉛、銻、石油、硫磺、雄黃等礦，亦接踵而起。

translations.literal: Copper, tin, lead, antimony, petroleum, sulfur, realgar, and other mines also rose one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Copper, tin, lead, antimony, petroleum, sulfur, realgar, and other mines followed in quick succession.

sentences.zh: 銅則雲南迤東湯丹、茂麓正廠六，子廠十一。

translations.literal: For copper: in eastern Yunnan, Tangdan and Maolu had six main works and eleven subsidiary works.
translations.idiomatic: Copper: in eastern Yunnan, Tangdan and Maolu had six main mines and eleven subsidiaries.

sentences.zh: 迤西回龍、得寶正廠八，子廠九。

translations.literal: In western Yunnan, Huilong and Debao had eight main works and nine subsidiary works.
translations.idiomatic: In western Yunnan, Huilong and Debao had eight main mines and nine subsidiaries.

sentences.zh: 楚雄永北及雲武所屬萬寶、雙龍，又永安順寧、臨安、開化、曲靖各廠，均招商承采。

translations.literal: Yongbei in Chuxiong and Wanbao and Shuanglong under Yunwu, also works at Yong'an, Shunning, Lin'an, Kaihua, and Qujing—all recruited merchants to undertake extraction.
translations.idiomatic: Yongbei in Chuxiong, Wanbao and Shuanglong under Yunwu, and mines at Yong'an, Shunning, Lin'an, Kaihua, and Qujing all recruited merchant contractors.

sentences.zh: 而江西贛州，陝西鎮安，湖南綏寧，新疆拜城、庫車亦有銅廠。

translations.literal: Moreover Ganzhou in Jiangxi, Zhen'an in Shaanxi, Suining in Hunan, and Baicheng and Kuche in Xinjiang also had copper works.
translations.idiomatic: Copper works also operated at Ganzhou in Jiangxi, Zhen'an in Shaanxi, Suining in Hunan, and Baicheng and Kuche in Xinjiang.

sentences.zh: 錫則廣東儋州，廣西南丹土州、富川、賀縣。

translations.literal: For tin: Danzhou in Guangdong; Nandan Native Prefecture, Fuchuan, and Hexian in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Tin: Danzhou in Guangdong; Nandan, Fuchuan, and Hexian in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 鉛則湖南常寧、湘鄉、臨武，四川會理，浙江鎮海、奉化、象山、寧海、太平。

translations.literal: For lead: Changning, Xiangxiang, and Linwu in Hunan; Huili in Sichuan; Zhenhai, Fenghua, Xiangshan, Ninghai, and Taiping in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Lead: Changning, Xiangxiang, and Linwu in Hunan; Huili in Sichuan; and Zhenhai, Fenghua, Xiangshan, Ninghai, and Taiping in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 銻則湖南益陽、邵陽、新化、沅陵、慈利、湘鄉、祁陽、新安、漵浦，貴州銅仁，四川秀山，廣東曲江、防城、乳源，廣西南太、泗鎮、陵陽都。

translations.literal: For antimony: Yiyang, Shaoyang, Xinhua, Yuanling, Cili, Xiangxiang, Qiyang, Xin'an, and Xupu in Hunan; Tongren in Guizhou; Xiushan in Sichuan; Qujiang, Fangcheng, and Ruyuan in Guangdong; Nantai, Sizhen, and Lingyangdu in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Antimony: Hunan (Yiyang, Shaoyang, Xinhua, Yuanling, Cili, Xiangxiang, Qiyang, Xin'an, Xupu); Tongren in Guizhou; Xiushan in Sichuan; Qujiang, Fangcheng, and Ruyuan in Guangdong; and Nantai, Sizhen, and Lingyangdu in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 石油則陝西延長，甘肅玉門，新疆庫爾喀喇烏蘇。

translations.literal: For petroleum: Yanchang in Shaanxi, Yumen in Gansu, and Kuerkala Wusu in Xinjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Petroleum: Yanchang in Shaanxi, Yumen in Gansu, and Kuerkala Wusu in Xinjiang.

sentences.zh: 硫磺則山西陽曲，奉天遼陽、錦州。

translations.literal: For sulfur: Yangqu in Shanxi; Liaoyang and Jinzhou in Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: Sulfur: Yangqu in Shanxi; Liaoyang and Jinzhou in Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 雄黃則湖南慈利。

translations.literal: For realgar: Cili in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Realgar: Cili in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 或官辦，或商辦，或官商合辦。

translations.literal: Some were run by the state, some by merchants, some jointly by state and merchants.
translations.idiomatic: Operations were government-run, merchant-run, or joint ventures.

sentences.zh: 或用土法，或用西法。

translations.literal: Some used native methods, some Western methods.
translations.idiomatic: Some used traditional methods, others Western technology.

sentences.zh: 九年，詔各省煤礦招商集股舉辦。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, an edict ordered each province's coal mines to recruit merchants and raise shares jointly to undertake operations.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 9 an edict called on provinces to develop coal mines through merchant investment and shareholding.

sentences.zh: 自是雲南、四川均設招商及礦務局，貴州設礦務公商局，山西設礦務公司。

translations.literal: From this Yunnan and Sichuan each established merchant-recruitment and mining affairs bureaus; Guizhou established a public-merchant mining affairs bureau; Shanxi established a mining affairs company.
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan and Sichuan set up merchant-recruitment and mining bureaus; Guizhou a public-merchant mining bureau; and Shanxi a mining company.

sentences.zh: 粵東瓊州之銅礦，浙江寧波之鉛礦，皆率招商集股開辦。

translations.literal: Copper mines at Qiongzhou in eastern Guangdong and lead mines at Ningbo in Zhejiang both generally recruited merchants and raised shares to open operations.
translations.idiomatic: Copper mines at Qiongzhou in Guangdong and lead mines at Ningbo in Zhejiang were opened through merchant syndicates.

sentences.zh: 開辦曆數十年，惟開平、萍鄉之煤，大冶之鐵，規模宏遠。

translations.literal: Operations had lasted several decades; only coal at Kaiping and Pingxiang and iron at Daye had far-reaching scale.
translations.idiomatic: After decades of operation, only Kaiping and Pingxiang coal and Daye iron had achieved true scale.

sentences.zh: 次則平江之金，益陽之銻，常寧之鉛，猶為民利。

translations.literal: Next, gold at Pingjiang, antimony at Yiyang, and lead at Changning still benefited the people.
translations.idiomatic: Gold at Pingjiang, antimony at Yiyang, and lead at Changning also served the public good, though on a smaller scale.

sentences.zh: 漠河金礦所產雖富，歲解部銀僅二十萬兩。

translations.literal: Although the Mohe gold mine's output was rich, yearly tribute silver remitted to the Board was only two hundred thousand taels.
translations.idiomatic: Despite rich output, the Mohe gold mine sent only two hundred thousand taels a year to the capital.

sentences.zh: 滇銅自十三年命唐蜅督辦，歲運京銅不過百餘萬，各省鼓鑄，猶以重直購洋銅。

translations.literal: Since the thirteenth year, when Tang Yu was ordered to supervise Yunnan copper, yearly copper transported to the capital did not exceed slightly over one million; each province's coin casting still paid high prices to purchase foreign copper.
translations.idiomatic: Since Tang Jiong was put in charge in Guangxu 13, Yunnan copper shipped to Beijing never exceeded about one million jin; provinces still paid premium prices for imported copper to keep mints running.

sentences.zh: 鐵產為漢陽廠鍊鋼造軌，略供輪路之需。

translations.literal: Iron output was refined into steel and rails at the Hanyang works, roughly supplying railway needs.
translations.idiomatic: Hanyang's steelworks turned iron into rails, barely meeting railway demand.

sentences.zh: 粵、桂、晉出鐵雖饒，以提鍊不精，國內製造，仍多購自英廠。

translations.literal: Although iron output from Guangdong, Guangxi, and Shanxi was abundant, because refining was not precise, domestic manufacturing still mostly purchased from British mills.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong, Guangxi, and Shanxi produced plenty of iron, but poor refining meant domestic industry still relied heavily on British mills.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，詔設礦務鐵路總局於京師，以王文韶、張廕桓主之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, an edict established the General Bureau of Mining Affairs and Railways at the capital, with Wang Wenshao and Zhang Yinhuan presiding.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 24 a General Bureau of Mining and Railways was established in Beijing under Wang Wenshao and Zhang Yinhuan.

sentences.zh: 奏定章程二十二，准華商辦礦，假貸洋款，及華洋合股，設立公司。

translations.literal: Twenty-two regulations were memorialized and fixed, permitting Chinese merchants to operate mines, borrow foreign loans, and form Chinese-foreign joint-stock companies.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-two regulations were approved, allowing Chinese merchants to mine, borrow foreign capital, enter Sino-foreign partnerships, and form companies.

sentences.zh: 自是江西萍鄉煤礦則借德款，湖北大冶鐵礦則借日本款，浙江寶昌公司則借義款，直隸臨城煤礦則借比款。

translations.literal: From this Jiangxi's Pingxiang coal mine borrowed German funds; Hubei's Daye iron mine borrowed Japanese funds; Zhejiang's Baochang Company borrowed Italian funds; Zhili's Lincheng coal mine borrowed Belgian funds.
translations.idiomatic: Pingxiang coal in Jiangxi took German loans; Daye iron in Hubei Japanese loans; Baochang Company in Zhejiang Italian loans; and Lincheng coal in Zhili Belgian loans.

sentences.zh: 當其議定合同，於抵押息金外，輒須延聘礦師，甚者涉及用人管理。

translations.literal: When contracts were negotiated, beyond mortgaged interest payments they invariably had to hire foreign mining engineers; in severe cases this extended to staffing and management.
translations.idiomatic: Loan contracts went beyond interest and collateral—foreign engineers had to be hired, and in the worst cases they controlled personnel and management.

sentences.zh: 至直隸井陘、安徽宣城煤礦，山西盂平、澤、潞、平陽，四川江北煤鐵礦，新疆塔城，直隸霍家地、廠子溝金礦，廣西上思，貴州正安鉛鐵，福建邵武、建寧、汀州，直隸八道河，奉天尾明山，及吉林新舊礦，均華洋合辦，一經訂約，時生轇轕。

translations.literal: As for coal mines at Jingxing in Zhili and Xuancheng in Anhui; coal and iron in Yu, Ping, Ze, Lu, and Pingyang in Shanxi; coal and iron in Jiangbei, Sichuan; Tacheng in Xinjiang; gold mines at Huojiadi and Changzigou in Zhili; lead and iron at Shangsi in Guangxi and Zheng'an in Guizhou; mines at Shaowu, Jianning, and Tingzhou in Fujian; Badaohe in Zhili; Weimingshan in Fengtian; and old and new mines in Jilin—all were Chinese-foreign joint operations; once contracts were drawn, disputes constantly arose.
translations.idiomatic: Chinese-foreign joint ventures at Jingxing coal in Zhili, Xuancheng in Anhui, Shanxi's Yu-Ping-Ze-Lu-Pingyang coal and iron, Jiangbei in Sichuan, Tacheng in Xinjiang, Huojiadi and Changzigou gold in Zhili, Shangsi and Zheng'an lead and iron, Fujian's Shaowu-Jianning-Tingzhou mines, Badaohe in Zhili, Weimingshan in Fengtian, and old and new Jilin mines all led to recurring disputes once contracts were signed.

sentences.zh: 若福公司之於晉礦，其尤甚者也。

translations.literal: As for the Fu Company in relation to Shanxi mining, this was especially severe.
translations.idiomatic: The Fu Company's grip on Shanxi mining was the worst case of all.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，河南豫豐公司以其專辦懷慶左右黃河以北各礦之權，山西商務局以其專辦盂平、澤、潞、平陽煤鐵各礦之權，同時讓與辦理。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, Henan's Yufeng Company, with its exclusive right to operate all mines north of the Yellow River around Huaiqing, and Shanxi's Bureau of Commerce, with its exclusive right to operate coal and iron mines in Yu, Ping, Ze, Lu, and Pingyang, simultaneously transferred those rights for operation.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 24 Henan's Yufeng Company—holding exclusive rights to mines north of the Yellow River around Huaiqing—and Shanxi's Bureau of Commerce—holding rights to coal and iron in Yu, Ping, Ze, Lu, and Pingyang—simultaneously transferred their concessions.

sentences.zh: 一公司壟斷兩省礦務，更議修鐵道自晉訖汴，因礦及路，利權損失，爭持三年，始允合辦。

translations.literal: One company monopolized mining affairs of two provinces and further proposed building a railway from Shanxi to Bian; linking mine and rail, sovereign interests were lost; dispute lasted three years before joint operation was finally permitted.
translations.idiomatic: A single company monopolized mining in two provinces and proposed a railway from Shanxi to Kaifeng; linking mines to rails cost China dearly; after three years of dispute joint operation was grudgingly allowed.

sentences.zh: 汴既侵攘華官主權，晉復干涉人民開採。

translations.literal: At Bian the Chinese official sovereignty was already encroached upon; at Shanxi it again interfered with the people's opening and extraction.
translations.idiomatic: In Henan it eroded Chinese official authority; in Shanxi it interfered with local mining.

sentences.zh: 全晉紳民，堅持廢約。

translations.literal: Gentry and people throughout Shanxi firmly insisted on abrogating the contract.
translations.idiomatic: Shanxi gentry and commoners united to demand cancellation of the contract.

sentences.zh: 遲之又久，始以銀二百七十餘萬贖回。

translations.literal: After long delay, at last over 2.7 million taels of silver were paid to buy it back.
translations.idiomatic: Only after prolonged delay was the concession bought back for more than 2.7 million taels.

sentences.zh: 他如陝西延長，四川富順、巴、萬石油礦，湖南常寧龍王山，湖北興國龍角山礦，均因商民私相授受，釀成交涉。

translations.literal: Others such as petroleum mines at Yanchang in Shaanxi, Fushun, Ba, and Wan in Sichuan, Dragon King Mountain in Changning, Hunan, and Dragon Horn Mountain in Xingguo, Hubei—all because merchants and people privately transferred rights among themselves, producing diplomatic disputes.
translations.idiomatic: Similar disputes arose over oil at Yanchang in Shaanxi and Fushun, Ba, and Wan in Sichuan; mines at Dragon King Mountain in Changning, Hunan, and Dragon Horn Mountain in Xingguo, Hubei—all from private transfers among merchants that led to diplomatic rows.

sentences.zh: 自議訂膠濟、東清路約，附路十三里內華人無開礦權。

translations.literal: Since the Jiaoji and Eastern Qing railway agreements were negotiated, within thirteen li adjoining the lines Chinese had no right to open mines.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiaoji and Eastern Qing railway treaties barred Chinese from mining within thirteen li of the tracks.

sentences.zh: 而開平煤礦，漠河觀音山金礦，復因內亂為外人所侵佔。

translations.literal: Moreover the Kaiping coal mine and the Mohe Guanyin Mountain gold mine were again seized by foreigners because of internal disorder.
translations.idiomatic: The Kaiping coal mine and Mohe's Guanyin Mountain gold mine were also seized by foreigners during domestic turmoil.

sentences.zh: 開平煤礦，自光緒元年直隸總督李鴻章集官商之力，經營二十年，效力大著。

translations.literal: The Kaiping coal mine, from Guangxu 1 when Zhili governor-general Li Hongzhang gathered official and merchant strength, was operated twenty years with great effect shown.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang had organized Kaiping as a joint official-merchant venture in Guangxu 1; after twenty years it was highly successful.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，拳匪亂後，洋員德璀琳因督辦張翼委其保護，與礦師胡華私立賣約，而張翼亦即籤押移交，轉以加招洋股中外合辦奏聞。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, after the Boxer turmoil, the foreign employee Detring, because supervisor Zhang Yi entrusted protection to him, privately drew up a sale contract with mining engineer Hoover; Zhang Yi also signed and transferred; then, adding foreign shares for Chinese-foreign joint operation, this was memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: After the Boxer uprising in Guangxu 26, foreign adviser Detring—entrusted by supervisor Zhang Yi to protect the mine—signed a secret sale with engineer Hoover; Zhang signed it over and reported a Sino-foreign joint venture with expanded foreign shares.

sentences.zh: 由是而唐山西山、半壁店、馬家溝、無水庄、趙各庄、林西各礦，秦皇島口岸地畝附屬之承平、建平、永平金銀礦，悉操於英公司。

translations.literal: Hence Tangshan's Xishan, Banbodian, Majiagou, Wushuizhuang, Zhaogezhuang, and Linxi mines, and the Chengping, Jianping, and Yongping gold and silver mines attached to Qinhuangdao port lands—all came under control of the British company.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter British interests controlled Tangshan mines at Xishan, Banbodian, Majiagou, Wushuizhuang, Zhaogezhuang, and Linxi, plus the Chengping, Jianping, and Yongping gold and silver mines tied to the Qinhuangdao port.

sentences.zh: 嚴詔責令收回，赴英控訴，卒未就緒。

translations.literal: Stern edicts ordered recovery; suit was brought in Britain; in the end it was not settled.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial orders demanded recovery and a lawsuit was filed in Britain, but the matter was never resolved.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，籌辦灤州煤礦，英公司阻撓之。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year, when planning the Luanzhou coal mine, the British company obstructed it.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 34 plans for the Luanzhou coal mine were blocked by the British company.

sentences.zh: 乃劫為營業聯合之法，合設開灤總局。

translations.literal: Thereupon it was forced into a business-union method, jointly establishing the Kaiping-Luan Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: A compromise joint venture was imposed, creating the Kailuan Mining Administration.

sentences.zh: 觀音山金礦，亦因拳亂為俄人佔據。

translations.literal: The Guanyin Mountain gold mine also, because of the Boxer turmoil, was occupied by Russians.
translations.idiomatic: Guanyin Mountain gold mine was also seized by Russians during the Boxer crisis.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，始以俄銀萬二千盧布贖回。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year, at last it was bought back with twelve thousand Russian rubles.
translations.idiomatic: It was finally repurchased in Guangxu 32 for twelve thousand rubles.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，外務部改定礦章，凡華洋商人得一體承辦礦務，惟必稟部批准，乃為允行之據。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs revised the mining regulations: all Chinese and foreign merchants could equally undertake mining affairs, but memorial to the ministry for approval was required as the basis for permitted operation.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 28 the Ministry of Foreign Affairs revised mining law: Chinese and foreign merchants could operate mines on equal terms, but only with ministry approval.

sentences.zh: 是年皖撫聶緝槼許英人凱約翰承辦歙、銅陵、大通、寧國、廣德、潛山礦產，嗣以專辦銅陵之銅官山，訂約定期百年，佔地三十八萬四千餘畝。

translations.literal: That year Anhui governor Nie Zhigui permitted the Englishman Caldwell to undertake mining at She, Tongling, Datong, Ningguo, Guangde, and Qianshan; afterward it was narrowed to Tongling's Tongguanshan exclusively; a contract was drawn for a term of one hundred years, occupying over three hundred eighty-four thousand mu of land.
translations.idiomatic: That year Anhui governor Nie Zhigui granted the Englishman Caldwell rights to mines at She, Tongling, Datong, Ningguo, Guangde, and Qianshan—later narrowed to Tongguanshan in Tongling—under a hundred-year lease covering more than 384,000 mu.

sentences.zh: 皖中紳民合力爭之，始以銀四十萬兩贖回自辦。

translations.literal: Gentry and people throughout Anhui jointly struggled against it; at last four hundred thousand taels of silver were paid to buy back and operate independently.
translations.idiomatic: Anhui gentry and citizens mobilized against it and bought the concession back for four hundred thousand taels to run themselves.

sentences.zh: 法人彌樂石亦於是年以勘辦全滇礦務請於滇督及外務部，皆拒之，仍獲澂江、臨安、開化、雲南、楚雄、元江、永北等府、廳、州礦權以去。

translations.literal: The Frenchman Milie also that year requested from the Yunnan governor and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs to survey and operate all Yunnan mining affairs; all refused him, yet he still obtained mining rights in the prefectures, departments, and subprefectures of Chenjiang, Lin'an, Kaihua, Yunnan, Chuxiong, Yuanjiang, and Yongbei and departed.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Frenchman Milie petitioned the Yunnan governor and Foreign Ministry to survey all Yunnan mining; though rebuffed at the top, he still walked away with rights in Chenjiang, Lin'an, Kaihua, Yunnan, Chuxiong, Yuanjiang, Yongbei, and other districts.

sentences.zh: 繼是英商立樂德以合辦東、昭兩府金銀礦不獲，遂援彌樂石例，索廣南、曲靖、麗江、大理、順寧、普洱、永昌七府礦，亦堅拒未允。

translations.literal: Next the English merchant Raede, failing to obtain joint operation of gold and silver mines in the two prefectures of Dong and Zhao, then invoked the Milie precedent, demanding mines of the seven prefectures Guangnan, Qujing, Lijiang, Dali, Shunning, Pu'er, and Yongchang; this too was firmly refused and not granted.
translations.idiomatic: English merchant Raede then failed to partner on gold and silver mines in Dong and Zhao prefectures; citing Milie's precedent, he demanded seven prefectures—Guangnan, Qujing, Lijiang, Dali, Shunning, Pu'er, and Yongchang—and was firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 一時舉國上下，咸以保全礦產為言。

translations.literal: For a time throughout the country above and below, all spoke of preserving mineral resources.
translations.idiomatic: For a time the whole country rallied around preserving mineral resources.

sentences.zh: 由是蜀設保富公司，華洋承辦川省礦務，購地轉租事宜屬之。

translations.literal: Hence Sichuan established the Baofu Company; Chinese and foreign parties undertaking Sichuan mining affairs, matters of land purchase and sublease were entrusted to it.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan therefore set up the Baofu Company to handle Sino-foreign mining ventures and land purchase and leasing.

sentences.zh: 閩設商政局，旋奏設礦務總公司，凡請辦各礦場，查核准駁之權屬之。

translations.literal: Fujian established a bureau of commercial administration; soon it memorialized to establish a general mining company, to which belonged the power to investigate, approve, and reject all petitions to operate mining sites.
translations.idiomatic: Fujian created a commercial bureau and then a general mining company with authority to approve or reject all mining applications.

sentences.zh: 山西保晉公司，安徽礦務總局，類能集合殷富，鳩貲開辦。

translations.literal: Shanxi's Baojin Company and Anhui's general mining bureau were alike able to gather wealthy backers and pool funds to open operations.
translations.idiomatic: Shanxi's Baojin Company and Anhui's mining bureau both pooled capital from wealthy investors to launch operations.

sentences.zh: 湘、鄂則於所屬礦地勘明圈購，以杜私售。

translations.literal: Hunan and Hubei then surveyed and marked out mining lands under their jurisdiction for purchase, to stop private sale.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan and Hubei surveyed and preemptively purchased mining lands under their jurisdiction to block private sales.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，江南籌辦農工礦路各學堂，兩湖復籌設高等礦業學堂。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, Jiangnan planned agricultural, industrial, mining, and railway schools; Liang-Hu again planned to establish advanced mining schools.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 25 Jiangnan planned schools for agriculture, industry, mining, and railways; Hunan and Hubei planned advanced mining academies.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，商部以洋商私占礦地礦山，疏請申明約章，以維權限。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year, the Ministry of Commerce, because foreign merchants privately occupied mining lands and mountains, memorialized requesting clarification of treaty provisions to preserve authority.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 31 the Ministry of Commerce, citing foreign encroachment on mines, asked that treaty provisions be clarified to protect sovereignty.

sentences.zh: 尋奏設各省礦政調查局，以勘明全國礦產、嚴禁私賣為先務。

translations.literal: Soon it memorialized to establish provincial mining administration survey bureaus, taking surveying the nation's mineral resources and strictly forbidding private sale as the first tasks.
translations.idiomatic: It then proposed provincial mining survey bureaus to map national resources and strictly ban unauthorized sales.

sentences.zh: 鄂督張之洞條上礦務正章七十四，附章七十三。

translations.literal: Hubei governor-general Zhang Zhidong submitted in articles seventy-four main mining regulations and seventy-three supplementary regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Hubei governor-general Zhang Zhidong submitted seventy-four main mining regulations with seventy-three supplementary articles.

sentences.zh: 蓋自二十四年以來，礦章屢易，每因礦務齟齬，洋商輒引為口實。

translations.literal: For since the twenty-fourth year mining regulations had repeatedly changed; whenever mining affairs caused friction, foreign merchants promptly cited them as pretexts.
translations.idiomatic: Mining regulations had changed repeatedly since Guangxu 24; foreign merchants seized every dispute as a pretext.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，商約大臣呂海寰與各國議訂商約，許以開採礦產之利，但必須遵守中國礦章。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, treaty commercial commissioner Lü Haihuan negotiated commercial treaties with the various nations, granting the benefit of opening and extracting mineral resources, but they must obey China's mining regulations.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 29 commercial commissioner Lü Haihuan negotiated treaties granting mining rights—but only under Chinese mining law.

sentences.zh: 而中國礦章，則比較各國通行者為之準則，特詔張之洞擬定。

translations.literal: China's mining regulations, however, were to take those in force among the various nations as standards for comparison; Zhang Zhidong was specially ordered to draft them.
translations.idiomatic: Chinese mining law was to be drafted by Zhang Zhidong using international standards as reference.

sentences.zh: 乃取英、美、德、法、比利時、西班牙礦章參互考證，區別地面地腹，釐定礦界礦稅，分晰地股銀股，暨華洋商，限制至周；

translations.literal: Then taking the mining regulations of Britain, America, Germany, France, Belgium, and Spain, cross-referencing and verifying them, distinguishing surface and subsurface, fixing mining boundaries and mining taxes, clarifying land shares and silver shares, together with Chinese and foreign merchants—restrictions were defined with thoroughness;
translations.idiomatic: Drawing on British, American, German, French, Belgian, and Spanish mining codes, he distinguished surface from subsurface rights, set boundaries and taxes, defined land and capital shares, and imposed exhaustive limits on Chinese and foreign operators—

sentences.zh: 尤注重於中國主權，華民生計，地方治理。

translations.literal: Especially emphasizing Chinese sovereignty, the livelihood of the Chinese people, and local governance.
translations.idiomatic: with special emphasis on sovereignty, Chinese livelihoods, and local administration.

sentences.zh: 閱數年乃成，下部議行，中國礦章始具云。

translations.literal: After several years it was completed, sent down to ministries for debate and implementation; China's mining regulations were then complete.
translations.idiomatic: Completed after several years and sent to ministries for enactment, China's mining code was finally in place.
